free, by topological order - each node's steady rate is a function of its
upstream nodes' rates alone, so solving in order gives one and only one
solution whatever the taus.

That matters because P3.4's contraction certificate, which P5.1's
serotonin circuit was built to satisfy, **is not satisfied here**:
`kappa = sigma_max(diag(g/4) W) = 1.414`. Satisfying it would have meant
weights of 0.707 or below, which buys nothing this network does not
already have and costs the legibility of unit weights. The certificate is
sufficient, not necessary, and this is the first place in the codebase
where the distinction does real work. So the test asserts *both* that
`kappa >= 1` and that `W**7 == 0`, and runs `stability.assess` to confirm
convergence, uniqueness across five initial conditions, local stability
and non-saturation empirically as well. Writing down "the certificate
fails and here is the stronger argument that replaces it" is the point;
quietly rescaling the weights until `kappa < 1` would have hidden it.

The same observation applies retrospectively to every hand-built
basal-ganglia scenario in this codebase, all of which are cascades, and it
is why they were fine without a certificate nobody had computed for them
yet.

### One start-up detail that is not cosmetic

`Simulation.run` starts from zero rates by default. On a network built to
rest at 0.5 that means the first minutes of every trace are a start-up
transient rather than a drug effect, and comparisons between conditions
are then differences of two transients. `dopamine.rest_rates()` returns
the fixed point and every test and the example pass it as `rates0`, so the
drug-free trace is exactly flat to 1e-6 and every deviation is the drug. A
test asserts that flatness, which is what makes the small effects below
(the second-order cortical-drive residual, the segregation check) legible
at all.

### What the model says, and the result the brief asked for

All of these are qualitative direction checks, on an illustrative circuit,
against the direct/indirect model - not fits.

**The pathways oppose each other, tested as a statement about pathways.**
[Kravitz2010] is optogenetics, not pharmacology: exciting direct-pathway
MSNs increased locomotion, exciting indirect-pathway MSNs produced
freezing and bradykinesia. So it is tested by adding drive to each MSN
node directly with no ligand anywhere, which is as close as a rate model
gets to channelrhodopsin. Direct up raises the readout; indirect up lowers
it.

**A D1 agonist and a D2 antagonist move one readout in opposite
directions.** Against a 1000 nM dopamine background on the shared network,
1000 nM dihydrexidine raises the locomotor readout from 0.6055 to 0.8094
and 200 nM haloperidol lowers it to 0.5545. Both are the direction the pathway each
drug acts on predicts. This is the acceptance criterion, and it is one
`solve_ivp` call over one state vector.

**Given together they partly cancel**, landing between the two
single-drug results - the thing two separate models cannot produce,
because the cancellation happens at the shared GPi node and nowhere else.

**Cortical drive alone almost does not move the output.** A perturbation
of the shared corticostriatal input drives both MSN populations
identically, and their two paths to GPi have opposite net sign, so to
first order at the operating point the output nucleus does not move at
all: a 0.097 shift in both MSNs produces a 0.0024 shift in GPi, 2.5% of
it. The residual is second order, because the direct path passes through
one sigmoid and the indirect through three. This is a consequence of rules
1 and 2 rather than a claim about the brain, and it is stated that way -
but it is the reason the scenario is about dopamine acting
*differentially* on two populations rather than about drive.

### The one result readers expect to be opposite and is not

D1 and D2 agonism are **not** opposing on locomotion in this model, and
should not be. D1 activation excites the direct MSN, which inhibits GPi;
D2 activation inhibits the indirect MSN, which via GPe -| STN also ends up
inhibiting GPi. Opposite receptor-level signs, one direction at the output.
A test asserts exactly that - opposite signs at the two striatal
populations, one sign at GPi - because it is the kind of thing that would
otherwise get "fixed" by someone who remembered "D1 and D2 oppose each
other" without remembering what they oppose each other *at*. The
oppositions that are real here are between pathway activations
([Kravitz2010]) and between a D1 agonist and a D2 antagonist.

There is one further genuine D1-versus-D2 opposition, and this model
cannot express it: D2 autoreceptors on nigrostriatal terminals and on
SNc/VTA somata, where an agonist reduces dopamine release, which is the
mechanism behind the biphasic locomotor dose-response of D2 agonists. It
is blocked for exactly the reason P5.1's 5-HT1A autoreceptor was:
`Simulation`'s ligand concentrations come from the PK layer and no circuit
rate has a path back into them. P5.1's
`test_autoreceptor_is_an_open_loop_until_phase_6` already asserts that gap
in general form, so it is recorded here and not re-asserted.

### Searched and empty

- **Binding kinetics for SCH-23390 at D1.** Searched Europe PMC for
  "SCH 23390" crossed with "dissociation rate constant", "koff" and
  "residence time"; for D1 with "TR-FRET", "NanoBRET" and "association
  rate constant"; and through the Rinken group's D1 work, which is the
  same group [Parkel2006] came from in P5.1. Allikalt A, Kopanchuk S,
  Rinken A (Eur J Pharmacol 2018;839:40-46) report association and
  dissociation half-lives of 40 s and 70 s and Kd 5.2 nM - for the
  FLUORESCENT ligand BodipyFL-SKF83566, not for SCH-23390. Farrell CB,
  O'Boyle KM (Eur J Pharmacol 1994;268(1):79-88) is the obvious source,
  measures [3H]SCH 23390 dissociation from rat striatum, and is paywalled
  with an abstract that reports the *effect of dopamine on* k-1 without
  reporting k-1. Billard W et al. (Life Sci 1984;35:1885-1893) gives the
  saturation Kd (0.53 nM, rat striatum) that derivation 3 uses instead.
- **Rodent pharmacokinetics for dihydrexidine and SCH-23390.** Searched
  each compound crossed with "pharmacokinetics", "half-life", "plasma
  concentration" and "brain concentration" in rat and mouse. Nothing
  usable: dihydrexidine's hits are in-vitro pharmacology and reviews of
  tavapadon; SCH-23390's are studies using it as a tool at a stated mg/kg
  without measuring its disposition. Both therefore share ONE illustrative
  `ke`, deliberately the same number as P5.1's
  `serotonin.TOOL_COMPOUND_KE`, for P5.1's stated reason - two invented
  values would assert a clearance ORDERING nothing supports. A test
  asserts the two constants are equal so they cannot drift apart, and
  another asserts this module's dopamine `ke` equals the D2 set's, because
  one dopamine dose is applied to both systems by name and the alternative
  is one molecule with two elimination rate constants.
- **A locomotor dose-response usable as a circuit-layer target.** Not
  searched again: Track E and P2.2 already established the blocker for
  this whole drug class, which is that behavioural pharmacology reports
  mg/kg by IP/SC/PO and this codebase has no such kinetics for these
  compounds. Phase 1's bridge is where such a dataset enters.

### What was deliberately not built

- **A cortico-thalamo-cortical feedback edge.** `Thalamus -> Cortex_M1`
  exists anatomically, and adding it turns the acyclic cascade into a loop
  whose gain nothing in reach fixes - and the uniqueness argument above goes with it,
  since `kappa = 1.414` means the contraction certificate would not cover
  the loop either.
- **An atlas-derived density factor.** `Drd1` is already in
  `expression/genes.py` tagged P5.2, `Drd2` is already in the model, P4.3
  scored both as striatum-dominant, and the two mechanism gains are
  explicitly the `mechanism_gain` half of P4.2's
  `coupling = mechanism_gain * rho[region]`. Two measured facts stop the
  upgrade rather than one guessed one. First, `rho` is a per-REGION factor
  and here both receptors sit in the SAME region on two different CELL
  TYPES, which a regional ISH map cannot separate - a real limit of the
  P4.2 factorization at exactly this scenario. Second, the direct
  pathway's own anatomy is the terminal-field mismatch P4.3 already
  records as an expected FAILURE for `Drd1`: nigral D1 protein is on the
  terminals of striatonigral neurons whose somata, and so whose
  transcript, are in the caudoputamen, and P4.2 measured the resulting
  CP:SNr error at 32-fold. A transcript-derived `rho` for the direct
  pathway's output nucleus would be wrong by that factor, in a known
  direction. This scenario is therefore the one that would benefit most
  from a cell-type-resolved density source and is furthest from having
  one.
- **The connectome-ported version.** P3.3 established that the ported
  indirect pathway inverts, because Knox et al. give GPe a thalamic
  projection seven to nine times denser than GPi's and the Albin-DeLong
  diagram gives it none. That finding applies unchanged to the direct
  pathway's ported form and would need the cell-type-resolved striatal
  output P3.3's `Restriction` stands in for. This scenario is the diagram,
  and P3.3 already documents at length what the diagram is and is not.
- **Endogenous dopamine tone.** Without it an antagonist given alone is
  inert, as everywhere else here; real SCH-23390 and real haloperidol both
  suppress locomotion given alone. P6.2. The test that asserts inertness
  says so, so the day P6.2 lands the expectation is already written down.

### What this task changes, and what it does not

- **One new module, and no change to any existing model file.**
  `dopamine.py` is additive; `scenarios.py`, `engine.py`, `receptor.py`,
  `network.py` and `serotonin.py` are untouched. The only edit outside the
  new files is adding `dopamine` to the package exports.
- **The calibrated D2 parameter set is reused, not re-derived.**
  `d2_receptor_site_calibrated()` and `d2_pk_models_calibrated()` are the
  same objects; only the coupling gain differs, for the stated saturation
  reason. So the D1/D2 comparison is a comparison of two independently
  sourced parameter sets rather than of two sets fitted to make it come
  out.
- **No existing test changed, none skipped, marked slow or weakened, and
  no tolerance widened.** 21 new test items, all in the offline gate.
- **Three D1 ligands' binding constants and efficacies are
  literature-sourced**, one of the three efficacies fractional and
  measured, one antagonist `koff` derived by the codebase's stated
  derivation 3 and checked against an independent bracket.
- **The circuit remains illustrative and is labelled as such**, as in
  every scenario before Phase 7 - but its parameters now follow three
  rules with a rejection criterion attached to one of them, and the
  uniqueness argument for the network is written down and asserted rather
  than inherited.

---

## Phase 5: noradrenaline alpha1, alpha2 and beta (P5.3)

### The task, and the two things that made it different

P5.3 asks for three adrenoceptor families with cited binding constants for
noradrenaline, prazosin, clonidine, yohimbine and propranolol, a scenario
plus tests, and the alpha2 autoreceptor's role noted for Phase 6. The new
code is `src/neurocascade/noradrenaline.py`, its tests are
`tests/test_noradrenaline_scenario.py`, and the worked example is
`examples/noradrenaline_locus_coeruleus_cortex.py`.

Two things separate it from P5.1 and P5.2, and both turned out to matter
more than the extra receptor family did.

The first is that **the sourcing came out unusually well.** Every affinity in
this module comes from one laboratory's programme of whole-cell radioligand
binding on CHO cells expressing a single human adrenoceptor subtype - four
papers covering alpha1 agonists, alpha1 antagonists, alpha2 agonists and
alpha2 antagonists ([Proudman2021], [Proudman2020], [Proudman2022],
[Proudman2022b]) plus the same group's earlier beta papers ([Baker2010],
[Baker2005]). That is the [Volpe2011]-style same-preparation guarantee the
D2 section went looking for and could not find, extended across three
receptor families, so "noradrenaline prefers receptor X to receptor Y" is a
comparison rather than a quotation of two unrelated experiments. Three
separate binding-kinetics papers then supply rate constants at each of the
three sites ([Sykes2022], [Tanaka2004] + [Quinton2010], [Gerhardt1990]).

The second is that **the sourcing coming out well is what exposed two
problems that P5.1 and P5.2 could only assume away**: whether derivation 3
is true, and what the endogenous agonist's affinity actually is. Both are
below, and both changed the module.

### Derivation 3, checked for the first time, and refined

Derivation 3 ("share the site's one measured `kon` and set
`koff = kon * Kd`") has been used since the GABA-A section and its content
is an assumption: that ligands at one site associate at comparable rates.
P5.1 stated the assumption and could not check it, because 5-HT1A and
5-HT2A each had exactly one measured `kon`. [Sykes2022]'s beta1 panel has
eighteen, all from one preparation, one radioligand and one method, and it
says two things:

- **Across chemotypes the assumption is false.** `kon` at human beta1 spans
  8.47e6 (sotalol) to 1.97e9 M^-1 min^-1 (carvedilol), a factor of 230.
- **Within a chemotype it holds well.** The four catecholamine-like agonists
  in the panel land in a narrow band: isoprenaline 2.51e7, salbutamol
  1.96e7, formoterol 1.68e7, salmeterol 2.63e7, a factor of 1.6 across all
  four.

So derivation 3 is applied here in a refined form - **share the measured
`kon` of the ligand chemically closest to the one being derived, and say
which** - and the beta1 panel is the evidence for the refinement rather than
a place where it is assumed. Noradrenaline at beta1 therefore takes
isoprenaline's `kon` and not propranolol's, which is 51-fold faster in the
same table. A test asserts both halves of the panel claim, so the licence
for the refinement is in the suite rather than in this paragraph.

The two remaining shared `kon`s cross chemotypes and are labelled as the
weaker assumptions they are (noradrenaline at alpha1 borrows prazosin's, a
quinazoline; noradrenaline and clonidine at alpha2 borrow
p-iodoclonidine's, an imidazoline), which on the panel's evidence puts up to
~100-fold of uncertainty on those `koff` values. What that does NOT touch is
any equilibrium result, and it is worth being precise about why: derivation
3 sets `koff = kon * Kd`, so the measured affinity is reproduced exactly for
any shared `kon`, and the whole uncertainty lands on the timescale over
which occupancy approaches equilibrium. A test rebuilds a ligand with a
`kon` 100x away and asserts its Kd is unchanged. That is a clarification the
codebase should have written down three tasks ago.

### The strongest constant so far, and two papers inconsistent with themselves

Prazosin at alpha1 is the first parameter here that three independent
measurements agree on:

    kon  0.048 nM^-1 min^-1   intact rat tail artery, 4 C    [Tanaka2004]
    koff 0.043 min^-1         rat brain synaptosomes, RT     [Quinton2010]
    -> Kd 0.896 nM
    Kd   0.851 nM             human alpha1A in CHO, 37 C     [Proudman2020]

5.3% apart, across three preparations, two species and three temperatures,
with nothing fitted. It is derivation 1 assembled from two papers and
checked against a third, and it is the reason the alpha1 arm of this module
needs no apology.

The `koff` used is [Quinton2010]'s and not [Tanaka2004]'s, for two reasons
worth separating. The first is that [Quinton2010] measured it in RAT BRAIN,
which is the tissue this project is about; that paper is about a mamba-venom
toxin and the number comes from its control arm, the same "the control arm
is what this project needed" pattern [Satala2016] and [Denomme2024] set in
P5.1. The second is that [Tanaka2004]'s three numbers do not agree with each
other: it reports Kon 0.048, Koff 0.078 and a kinetic pKD of 9.3, but
0.078/0.048 is 1.63 nM, i.e. pKD 8.79 - a 3.2-fold internal inconsistency.
Rather than pick one of its two readings, the value adopted from elsewhere
is checked to lie BETWEEN them (0.024 implied by its pKD with its own kon,
against 0.078 measured), and a test asserts that bracket's arithmetic. Being
bracketed by the two readings of the paper the number was not taken from is
the same kind of check the P5.2 SCH-23390 derivation got from [Reader1989].

[Gerhardt1990] has the same defect in the same direction at alpha2 (its
`kon * Kd` is 4.8-fold faster than its reported `koff`), and is likewise
used for its `kon` only. Two of the three kinetics papers in this task being
internally inconsistent is worth recording as a fact about this literature:
a rate-constant pair quoted from a single 1980s-1990s binding paper should
be checked against that paper's own equilibrium number before it is trusted,
and neither of these two survives that check.

### The 10000-fold problem, and the rule that decided it

P5.1 met the affinity-state problem at 5-HT2A, where serotonin's published
affinity varied 250-fold with the radioligand's own pharmacology. At alpha2
it is two orders of magnitude worse:

    noradrenaline at human alpha2A, whole-cell competition against the
      antagonist [3H]-rauwolscine                          Kd 269153 nM
      [Proudman2022]
    noradrenaline at rat cortex alpha2 sites, saturation binding of
      (-)-3H-noradrenaline ITSELF                          Kd     27 nM
      [UPrichard1978]

Neither is wrong. An agonist radioligand labels the G-protein-coupled
high-affinity state; a competition curve against an antagonist radioligand
reports a weighted view of the whole population; and [Salama1982] shows the
balance moving with GTP and Mg2+ at these exact receptors in rat cortex,
while [Ernsberger1987] shows the same two-state behaviour at alpha1. The
mechanism is documented, which is what makes this a state problem rather
than a discrepancy.

`ReceptorSite` has one pool and one affinity per ligand, so one had to be
chosen, and the choice was made by **applying P5.1's own rule rather than a
new one**: the preparation should match the receptor being modelled. P5.1
used that rule to pick serotonin's live-cell affinity at 5-HT2A. Here the
modelled receptor is a somatodendritic autoreceptor on a G-protein-coupled
noradrenergic neuron in rodent brain, and rat cortical membranes with an
agonist radioligand are the closest available preparation to that, so the
same rule selects the OTHER kind of assay. A rule that picks the same answer
whatever the case is not doing any work; this one is.

`ligands_alpha2(affinity_state=...)` therefore builds both sets, the
agonist-state one is the default, and the tests assert the qualitative
results under both. Three costs, all recorded:

- **The alpha2 site is then not matched to the alpha1 and beta sites.** The
  cross-receptor comparison below is computed from the whole-cell constants
  at all three sites, which are all defined in the module, and asserted
  algebraically.
- **The state choice flips the answer to "which adrenoceptor does
  noradrenaline engage first".** Whole-cell: beta1 (1820 nM), then alpha1A
  (15488), then alpha2A (269153). Agonist-state at alpha2: alpha2A (27 nM)
  first, by a factor of 67 over beta1. Both orderings are published
  measurements and this module can produce either. That is the honest
  headline of the task, and it is tested as two explicit orderings rather
  than smoothed into one.
- **The whole-cell noradrenaline set cannot be integrated at all**, and that
  is measured rather than asserted. `koff = 0.48 * 269153 = 129194 min^-1`
  is a 0.3 ms relaxation; `Simulation.run` uses explicit RK45 over one
  shared state vector, whose stability limit then bounds the step for the
  whole system at ~2e-5 min. A noradrenaline-dosed 10-minute window that
  takes ~3 s under the default set did not finish in 240 s under this one.
  So whole-cell alpha2 results are asserted at the algebraic fixed point of
  `ReceptorSite.occupancy_rhs`, which is exact and cheap, and a test
  asserts the arithmetic of the stiffness itself so that the reason stays
  attached to the decision. This is the first concrete, quantified case for
  Phase 9's stiff or quasi-steady-state occupancy solver: it is not about
  network size, it is about a legitimately measured low-affinity ligand
  whose kinetics are three orders faster than the circuit's.

One smaller check fell out of the same reading. The IUPHAR/BPS Guide records
the published range for noradrenaline at human alpha2A as pKi 3.6-7.4. Its
loose end IS [Proudman2022]'s value rounded to one decimal place (-3.57 ->
3.6), and its tight end (39.8 nM) is 1.5-fold LOOSER than the rat-cortex
value, which lies just outside it - the expected direction, since the
Guide's range is human-receptor values. The test says that rather than the
tidier "the range brackets both", which was the first thing written and was
false.

### What the numbers turned out to say

**Noradrenaline's highest affinity in the matched panel is for beta1, not
for either alpha.** 1820 nM at beta1 against 15488 nM at alpha1A and 269153
nM at alpha2A. The textbook ordering - noradrenaline as a potent alpha
agonist and a weak beta agonist - is a statement about POTENCY, and the same
papers' functional columns give exactly that ordering:

    site     Kd (nM)   functional EC50/IC50 (nM)   intrinsic efficacy ratio
    alpha1A    15488    2.45  (Ca2+ mobilization)         3.80 log units
    beta1       1820   11.5   (cAMP accumulation)         2.20
    alpha2A   269153  251     (Gi, CRE-SPAP)              3.03

Affinity says beta1 first; potency says alpha1A first. The gap is receptor
reserve and signal amplification, and it is 3.8 log units at alpha1A. This
model's `activation = sum(occupancy * efficacy)` is linear in occupancy with
no amplification term, so it reproduces the affinity ordering and not the
potency ordering. That is the same limitation P5.2 flagged for dopamine's
530-fold-affinity-versus-31-fold-potency gap, one receptor family wider and
an order of magnitude larger, and both orderings are asserted in the tests
with the numbers above so that neither can be quietly forgotten.

**The claim survives the alpha1 subtype uncertainty, and is stated in the
form that does.** Noradrenaline's affinity spans 49-fold across the three
alpha1 subtypes (alpha1D 3311, alpha1A 15488, alpha1B 162181 nM), so the
MARGIN by which beta1 wins is subtype-dependent: 1.8-fold, 8.5-fold,
89-fold. The ORDERING is not - beta1 is tighter than all three. Prazosin,
by contrast, is essentially non-selective across the three (0.85 / 1.8 /
0.85 nM), which is what makes every prazosin result here
subtype-independent. Both facts are tested.

**Propranolol is the codebase's fourth antagonist and its second
FAST-dissociating one.** Measured `koff` 0.91 min^-1, residence time 1.1
min ([Sykes2022]). The set now reads: naloxone 2.375, propranolol 0.91,
WAY-100635 0.0078, SCH-23390 0.00389 min^-1 - three orders of magnitude of
antagonist kinetics, none of it chosen. Its two published beta1 affinities
differ 9.7-fold (kinetic 0.711 nM against whole-cell 6.92 nM), the kinetic
one is used because its rate constants are measured, and
`ligands_beta(propranolol_affinity="whole-cell")` builds the other so that
"no result turns on which" is tested rather than promised.

**Clonidine is a weak partial agonist and carries the widest efficacy
uncertainty in the codebase.** [Jasper1998] measures intrinsic activity 0.32
relative to noradrenaline in one [35S]GTPgammaS panel at cloned human
alpha2a; [Proudman2022]'s intrinsic efficacy ratios put it at 2.7% of
noradrenaline's; [Pohjanoksa1998] could not detect an alpha2A response to it
at all. Those three are one low-intrinsic-efficacy ligand read out in three
systems with different receptor reserve, not three disagreeing
measurements. 0.32 is used, for consistency with P5.1's and P5.2's Emax
ratios, and the constant's docstring says plainly that what
`Ligand.efficacy` formally wants is relative INTRINSIC efficacy and that the
two coincide only without reserve. Every result that needs clonidine to be
a weaker agonist than noradrenaline holds under all three readings.

### The result the task exists to produce, and the one it got backwards

**One transmitter dose moves two nodes in opposite directions.** A single
noradrenaline dose raises the cortical pyramidal node through alpha1 (Gq,
[McCormick1991]) and beta1 (Gs, [Madison1986]) and lowers the LC node
through the alpha2 autoreceptor (Gi, [Cedarbaum1977]). Three receptor
systems, three G proteins, one `solve_ivp` call over one state vector.

**The two cortical receptors are separable, and their relative sizes are a
prediction.** alpha1 and beta1 land on the SAME node with the SAME sign, so
the only way to show they are two receptors is to remove them one at a time:
prazosin takes 0.0033 of the 0.0502 cortical response and propranolol takes
0.0386, and together they remove 83% of it. The beta part being the larger
is not a parameter - the two mechanism gains are equal by construction -
it follows from noradrenaline binding beta1 8.5-fold more tightly than
alpha1A, i.e. from [Baker2010] against [Proudman2021].

**Clonidine suppresses the LC alone and RAISES it against a noradrenaline
background.** This was predicted backwards on the way in: the first version
of the open-loop test asserted that adding clonidine to noradrenaline would
suppress the LC further, and it failed. It should have: a partial agonist
competing with a full agonist for one pool is a functional ANTAGONIST.
Clonidine binds the alpha2 pool 4.6-fold more tightly than noradrenaline in
the default state (5.9 nM against 27 nM) and activates it 0.32 as well, so
it displaces occupancy worth 1.0 of activation and replaces it with
occupancy worth 0.32. The failure got its own test rather than a widened
tolerance, and the result is state-dependent in a way that is itself
informative: under the whole-cell set noradrenaline barely occupies the
alpha2 pool at the same dose, so there is nothing to displace and clonidine
suppresses instead. Both are asserted, the first by integration and the
second algebraically.

**Yohimbine reverses clonidine partially at an equimolar dose and further at
5x.** Yohimbine is only 1.8-fold tighter than clonidine in the default state
(3.31 against 5.9 nM) and 58-fold tighter in the whole-cell one, so the
reversal is graded and its magnitude is state-dependent while its direction
is not. A test that asserted complete reversal at an equimolar dose would
have been asserting the wrong pharmacology.

### The autoreceptor, and Phase 6 stated in the form that matters here

P5.1 asserts the open-loop gap in general form and P5.2 declined to
re-assert it. It is re-asserted here, because the LC alpha2 autoreceptor is
the case where the missing half IS the clinical effect: an alpha2 agonist
activates the somatodendritic autoreceptor, LC firing falls, and in a real
brain less noradrenaline is released across the entire forebrain
([Callado2000], [Berridge2003]) - which is how clonidine sedates and lowers
blood pressure. This model expresses the first half and not the second.

`test_the_autoreceptor_is_an_open_loop_until_phase_6` therefore asserts that
clonidine moves the LC node while the cortical noradrenaline concentration,
the cortical alpha1 and beta1 occupancies and the cortical firing rate are
unchanged. Two details in it are deliberate:

- It asserts only the SIZE of the LC change and not its sign, because
  against a noradrenaline background the sign is the partial-agonist one
  above.
- Its numeric tolerance is `solve_ivp`'s own default `rtol` of 1e-3, not
  P5.1's 1e-4, and the reason is stated rather than fitted: this module's
  fastest occupancy component runs at 743 min^-1 against ~1 min^-1 in the
  serotonin module, so the same step-placement difference samples a much
  steeper trace. The measured worst case is 8.9e-4 relative. A tolerance
  taken from the integrator's documented accuracy is a bound; one chosen to
  fit the number would not have been, and rule 5 is rule 5.
- It also asserts the STRUCTURAL reason, which is not a tolerance at all:
  every ligand's concentration is driven by a PK model whose right-hand side
  is a function of its own state only, so no circuit rate can reach it.
  P6.1 is exactly the change that replaces one of those with a release term
  depending on `LC_NA`, and that assertion is what will fail when it lands.

### The circuit, and the rule that had to change shape

Three nodes: `LC_NA` (locus coeruleus noradrenergic neurons, somatodendritic
alpha2A autoreceptor, no edges); `PFC_Pyramidal` (layer V prefrontal
pyramidal neurons, carrying BOTH alpha1 and beta1); `PFC_GABA` (local
interneurons, no receptor, providing the recurrent inhibition that makes the
pyramidal response finite). The cortical loop weights are P5.1's, unchanged,
because the microcircuit being represented is the same one and changing them
would have implied a difference no source supports; a test asserts the
equality against `serotonin.raphe_cortical_network` so neither can drift.

The missing LC -> cortex edge is P5.1's decision for P5.1's reason, and it is
stronger here: the LC's influence on a cortical pyramidal cell is
receptor-mediated and of both signs at once through three receptor families,
so one signed weight would double-count the receptor layer.

Rules 1 and 2 carry over intact (rest at rate 0.5 everywhere, contraction
number 0.9 < 1 so P3.4's global-uniqueness certificate holds - unlike P5.2's
acyclic cascade, where it fails at 1.414 and acyclicity does the work
instead; a test asserts both, because two networks in this codebase now hold
by different arguments).

**Rule 3 had to change shape, and that is the one genuinely new
circuit-layer finding.** P5.1's unit-magnitude rule is per RECEPTOR: a fully
occupied receptor bound by a full agonist shifts its node's input by one
unit. `PFC_Pyramidal` carries two excitatory receptors, so that rule puts
+2.0 on it at saturation, and +2.0 rails it - minimum sigmoid sensitivity
0.0044, below `stability.SATURATION_FLOOR` of 0.01, and a railed node stops
responding to the other receptor. So the unit budget is per NODE: alpha1 and
beta1 get +0.5 each, summing to exactly the one unit P5.1 allots, and the
LC's single receptor keeps magnitude -1.0. The test asserts both halves
including the counterfactual, with the 0.0044 in it, because a rule that
cannot reject a value is not a rule.

Splitting the budget equally is also what keeps the scenario honest: the two
cortical receptors are given the same gain by construction, so the
alpha1-versus-beta asymmetry in the result above comes from the published
binding constants and from nothing hand-set.

One consequence of the illustrative PK is worth stating because it bounds
every quantitative statement in the scenario. `NORADRENALINE_KE` is the same
flagged transmitter proxy `dopamine.DOPAMINE_KE` and
`serotonin.SEROTONIN_KE` are (5.0 min^-1, t1/2 8.3 s), so a noradrenaline
"dose" is gone before a tau = 1.5 min cortical node can follow it: the peak
cortical rate is 0.5502 where the same occupancy held constant would give
above 0.7. A test computes both and asserts the gap, so the size of the
understatement is on the record rather than implied. Tonic release is P6.2.

### Searched and empty, or found and deliberately not used

- **Binding kinetics for noradrenaline itself, at any adrenoceptor.**
  Searched Europe PMC for the catecholamines crossed with "association rate
  constant", "dissociation rate constant", "residence time", NanoBRET and
  TR-FRET, and through the kinetic panels that do exist for these receptors.
  Every panel found measures antagonists and synthetic agonists; the
  endogenous transmitter is in none of them. Hence derivation 3 at all three
  sites for noradrenaline, with the chemotype refinement above.
- **Binding kinetics for clonidine and yohimbine.** [Gerhardt1990] measures
  the analogue p-iodoclonidine and is used for its `kon`; nothing was found
  for either compound itself. The [3H]rauwolscine and [3H]RX821002
  characterizations report equilibrium constants, and where they report
  kinetics at all it is for the radioligand rather than for the competitor.
- **Rodent PK for prazosin, clonidine, yohimbine and propranolol: found,
  and deliberately not used.** Unlike P5.1's and P5.2's tool compounds these
  four are clinical drugs and rodent PK for them exists - a single
  intravenous dose of rac-propranolol in the rat gives a terminal half-life
  of ~2.3 h (PMID:8593256). It is recorded in the module and not used, for
  two reasons. What `drug_pk.py` and Phase 1 consume is a parameter set per
  route (F, ka, Vd, CL, and a brain partition), not a terminal half-life,
  and half-sourcing one of the four would put a real citation next to three
  invented numbers and thereby assert a clearance ORDERING nothing in reach
  supports. And nothing in a receptor-layer task depends on the elimination
  rate beyond "all four are still on board across the window". So all four
  share one illustrative `TOOL_COMPOUND_KE`, deliberately equal to P5.1's
  and P5.2's, with a test asserting the equality. This is a stronger record
  than P5.1's on the same subject, because it says the data exists and where
  it goes rather than reporting an empty search.
- **Noradrenaline's own clearance rate.** The same gap dopamine and
  serotonin have, for the same reason: NET-mediated reuptake is a saturable
  Michaelis-Menten transporter process on a sub-second timescale, not
  first-order elimination. P5.8 (NET) and P6.2 (endogenous tone) own it.
- **A behavioural dose-response usable as a circuit-layer target.** Not
  searched again; Track E and P2.2 established the blocker for the whole
  class and Phase 1's bridge is where such a dataset enters.

### What was deliberately not built

- **Postsynaptic alpha2A in the cortex.** It is really there and it matters:
  [Wang2007] shows alpha2A stimulation on pyramidal dendritic spines closing
  HCN channels and STRENGTHENING network connections, which is the
  guanfacine working-memory mechanism. That is P5.2's D1 problem in a new
  place - the receptor's cAMP sign is not in doubt, but its effect on a rate
  node is an increase in the efficacy of incoming input rather than a
  decrease in firing, and this engine has one scalar drive per node. Adding
  it would mean choosing that sign by hand with no measurement that settles
  it for a rate model. `alpha2` here is the autoreceptor only.
- **The subtype split.** All eight adrenoceptor genes are already in
  `expression/genes.py` tagged P5.3 and every affinity above is reported per
  subtype, so a subtype-resolved version is a table lookup away. It is not
  built because the three sites here are pharmacological pools rather than
  regions, and the question a split would answer (which subtype does the
  cortical pyramidal node carry?) is cell-type-resolved in a way a regional
  ISH map cannot answer - P5.2's limit, at a different scenario. What is
  done instead is to state every claim in the form that survives the subtype
  uncertainty and to test that it does.
- **An atlas-derived density factor.** Same position and same reason as P5.1
  and P5.2: the three mechanism gains are explicitly the `mechanism_gain`
  half of P4.2's `coupling = mechanism_gain * rho[region]`, and the
  committed expression fixture does not carry these genes, so a
  density-derived map would make every test in this module depend on the
  gitignored cache.
- **Endogenous noradrenergic tone.** Without it an antagonist given alone is
  inert, as everywhere else here; real prazosin, yohimbine and propranolol
  all have effects alone because a real LC fires tonically. P6.2, and the
  test that asserts inertness says so.
- **The imidazoline story.** Clonidine binds non-adrenergic I1 sites with an
  affinity comparable to its alpha2 one, which is why the mechanism of
  clonidine-like antihypertensives was argued about for two decades. A
  single-site alpha2 model cannot represent it, and the module says so, so
  that a clonidine result in this codebase is not read as a claim about the
  drug's mechanism in vivo.

### What this task changes, and what it does not

- **One new module, and no change to any existing model file.**
  `noradrenaline.py` is additive; `engine.py`, `receptor.py`, `network.py`,
  `scenarios.py`, `serotonin.py` and `dopamine.py` are untouched. The only
  edit outside the new files is adding `noradrenaline` to the package
  exports. Three receptor systems on one shared network needed no engine
  change, for the same reason two did.
- **Seven ligand-site pairs' binding constants and five ligands' efficacies
  are literature-sourced**, across three receptor families: six measured
  rate constants (prazosin's `kon` and `koff`, propranolol's `kon` and
  `koff`, isoprenaline's `kon`, p-iodoclonidine's `kon`) and every remaining
  `koff` derived by the stated derivation 3. One efficacy is fractional
  and measured (clonidine 0.32), one zero is measured (yohimbine), one
  "1.0" is measured rather than conventional (noradrenaline at beta1,
  102.4% of isoprenaline), and two zeros are the flagged inverse-agonism
  simplification (prazosin, propranolol).
- **No existing test changed, none skipped, marked slow or weakened.** 28
  new test items, all in the offline gate, running in ~63 s. Two tolerances
  in the new tests are set from the integrator's documented accuracy rather
  than from the numbers they have to admit, and both say so.
- **Two test expectations were wrong and were fixed as expectations**, not
  by adjusting the module: the alpha1/beta decomposition had the two
  antagonists' roles transposed, and the clonidine-against-noradrenaline
  direction was the partial-agonist one rather than the one assumed. The
  second became a test of its own.
- **The circuit and the pharmacokinetics remain illustrative and labelled**,
  as in every scenario before Phase 7 - but rule 3 now has a per-node form
  with a stated rejection criterion, and derivation 3 has a chemotype
  refinement with published evidence behind it, so two of this codebase's
  standing conventions are better founded than they were before this task.

## Phase 5: acetylcholine, nicotinic and muscarinic (P5.4)

### The task, and the one thing in it that is not a sourcing exercise

P5.1 to P5.3 were sourcing tasks: find the constants, write them down with
citations, wire a small illustrative circuit, and change no engine code.
P5.4 asks for the same for acetylcholine at two nicotinic and five
muscarinic receptors, and then adds a sentence that is not a sourcing
instruction at all:

> Nicotinic desensitization is pharmacologically central and cannot be
> represented by the existing two-state occupancy model: add a desensitized
> state, in the same way that GABA-A allosteric modulation required the
> `connection_modulation` mechanism.

So the interesting half of this task is a mechanism question, and the brief
names the precedent for how to answer it. The GABA-A section above records
the shape of that answer: before adding machinery, ask whether the existing
mechanism is the wrong SIZE or the wrong SHAPE, and only extend when it is
the wrong shape, because reusing a mechanism that has the wrong shape is a
dishonest shortcut wearing the costume of parsimony. That question is asked
three times here and answered three different ways.

### Question one: does nicotinic desensitization fit `ReceptorSite`?

No, and not marginally.

`ReceptorSite` is a two-state model. A receptor is free or it is bound to
one of the competing ligands, and `activation = sum(occ_i * efficacy_i)`.
"Occupied" and "active" are one variable, so activation is a monotone
increasing function of every ligand's concentration, always, for every
parameter set. There is no way to make it not be.

The defining fact about a nicotinic receptor is that this is false.
[Katz1957] established at the motor end-plate that acetylcholine drives the
receptor into a state that is still agonist-occupied and no longer
conducting, entered and left with its own rate constants. [Fenster1997]
measured those rate constants for the two neuronal subtypes modelled here,
in one laboratory, in one preparation, in one table, and reported the
consequence that makes desensitization pharmacologically central rather
than a second-order correction:

    nicotine at rat alpha4beta2, activation EC50        15 uM
    nicotine at rat alpha4beta2, desensitization IC50    0.061 uM

A 246-fold window in which nicotine's dominant action on this receptor is
to REMOVE it from the available pool rather than to activate it, and plasma
nicotine in a smoker sits inside that window. At alpha7 the same experiment
gives 90 uM against 1.3 uM, a 69-fold window. A model of acetylcholine
pharmacology that cannot express this does not have a small quantitative
error in it; it has the wrong sign of response over the concentration range
that matters most.

Three ways of faking it inside the two-state model were considered and
rejected, and it is worth recording why, because each is the sort of thing
that looks like parsimony:

- **Lower nicotine's `efficacy`.** Efficacy is a concentration-independent
  multiplier. Desensitization is concentration-dependent and
  time-dependent. Fitting an efficacy would reproduce a reduced response at
  one concentration and be wrong at every other, and it would make the
  receptor recover the instant the drug left, rather than over the 43 to 87
  minutes two experiments measured.
- **Give nicotine a second `Ligand` entry with a tighter affinity and zero
  efficacy**, competing with itself. This is closer, and it is the sort of
  trick that would have worked, in the sense of producing a
  bell-shaped-looking activation curve. It is wrong because the two
  populations would then be in instantaneous equilibrium with each other
  through the free pool rather than connected by the measured `k_des` and
  `k_rec`, so every timing result would be an artefact of the binding rates
  (which are illustrative here, see below) instead of the gating rates
  (which are measured). It also asserts that a desensitized receptor
  releases and re-binds its agonist, which is exactly the opposite of what
  makes the desensitized state the high-affinity one.
- **Treat desensitization as a `connection_modulation` gain.** The GABA-A
  mechanism scales a synapse's efficacy by `1 + gain * activation`. That
  represents a modulator acting on a synapse. Desensitization is not a
  modulator acting on anything: it is the receptor's own conformational
  state, and it competes for the same finite receptor pool the agonist
  binds.

So `receptor.py` gained `DesensitizingReceptorSite`, which is the
Katz-Thesleff cycle written per orthosteric ligand `i`:

```
free = 1 - sum(bound) - sum(desensitized)

d bound_i/dt        = kon_i*C_i*free - koff_i*bound_i
                      - k_des_i*bound_i + k_rec_i*desensitized_i
d desensitized_i/dt = k_des_i*bound_i - k_rec_i*desensitized_i

activation          = sum(bound_i * efficacy_i)
```

Three properties of that arrangement are load-bearing and each has a test:

1. **Desensitized receptor still occupies the pool.** It is subtracted from
   `free`, so a desensitized population keeps competing. Anything else
   would make a desensitizing agonist look as though it were vanishing from
   the receptor.
2. **Ligand does not dissociate directly from the desensitized state.**
   This is what makes the desensitized state the HIGH-affinity one, and it
   is not a modelling flourish: it produces, with no further assumption, an
   apparent equilibrium affinity of `Kd / (1 + k_des/k_rec)` for total
   binding. See "The prediction this makes" below, which is the most
   interesting result in this task.
3. **`k_des` is per ligand and may be zero.** An orthosteric competitive
   antagonist occupies the site without driving the conformational change,
   so it must be possible to say that. No such ligand is instantiated in
   P5.4 (dihydro-beta-erythroidine and methyllycaconitine are the obvious
   candidates and neither had constants in reach), but a site whose API
   cannot express it would have to be rebuilt the day one arrives.

### Question two: does mecamylamine fit the competitive pool?

No, and this is the GABA-A question again with a different answer to the
same test.

Mecamylamine is not a competitive antagonist. [Papke2001] states that its
inhibition of neuronal nicotinic receptors "was noncompetitive and voltage
dependent", and [Arias2010] locates its site in the channel lumen, "between
the non-polar (position 17') and outer (position 20') rings" of the
transmembrane domain, structurally distinct from the agonist site. Putting
it in `ReceptorSite`'s competitive pool would assert that it displaces
acetylcholine, which is the one thing it demonstrably does not do, and the
model would then predict that a high enough acetylcholine concentration
overcomes mecamylamine's block. Real non-competitive block is
insurmountable, which is the whole reason the distinction has a name.

`DesensitizingReceptorSite` therefore takes an optional second, independent
ligand pool:

```
d blocked_j/dt = konb_j*Cb_j*(1 - sum(blocked)) - koffb_j*blocked_j
activation     = (1 - sum(blocked)) * sum(bound_i * efficacy_i)
```

The multiplicative form is chosen because it reproduces exactly what a
functional IC50 for non-competitive inhibition measures: activation halved
when the blocker sits at its own Kd, at any agonist concentration. That is
tested directly, and so is the property that matters more, that the
agonist's occupancy is bit-for-bit unchanged by the blocker.

What this deliberately does not represent is the use- and
voltage-dependence of real open-channel block. This engine has no membrane
potential and no channel-open state for "use" to be a function of, so the
block here does not grow with agonist concentration and real block does.
That is stated in the module rather than left for a reader to discover.

### Question three: do the muscarinic receptors need the new state?

No, and that is a modelling claim made on purpose rather than a corner cut.
`M1` and `M2` are plain `ReceptorSite`s, and scopolamine sits in the
competitive pool with acetylcholine because scopolamine really does compete
for the orthosteric site, the same finding P5.1 recorded for
diazepam/flumazenil at the benzodiazepine site.

Muscarinic receptors do desensitize. They are G-protein-coupled, and their
agonist-induced desensitization is a phosphorylation/arrestin process
running over minutes to hours, with no rate constant in reach for
acetylcholine or scopolamine at any of the five subtypes. Nicotinic
desensitization is an intrinsic conformational change of the channel with
measured rate constants at both subtypes from one table. Giving the
muscarinic sites a desensitized state would have meant inventing two rate
constants per site, which rule 1 forbids, in order to represent a process
whose timescale barely overlaps this model's window.

The contrast between the two halves of `acetylcholine.py` is the point of
having them in one module: one transmitter, two receptor superfamilies,
four instantiated sites, and only two of them need the new state. If the
new state had been necessary for all four it would have been much weaker
evidence that it was necessary at all.

### The engine change, which is smaller than it sounds

Before P5.4, `Simulation` used one number per receptor system for two
different jobs: how many PK models and `doses` entries the system needs,
and how many rows of the shared state vector it owns. Those were the same
number because every site owned one occupancy per ligand. A desensitizing
site owns `2*n_orthosteric + n_blockers` states for `n_orthosteric +
n_blockers` ligands, so the two had to be separated:

- `ReceptorSite` gained an `n_states` attribute equal to `n`, so the engine
  needs no branch on site type, and `getattr(..., site.n)` keeps duck-typed
  external sites working.
- `Simulation` gained `n_ligands` (the `doses` length) alongside `r` (the
  occupancy-region length), a second offset table, and `state_rows(i)`.
- `receptor_site.occupancy_rhs` and `.activation` keep their signatures.
  They are handed the system's whole state block and its whole
  concentration vector, and the site decides what the block means. That is
  what kept the change to about thirty lines of `engine.py` code (the diff
  is larger only because of the comments that explain them): the engine
  does not know that desensitization exists.

For every scenario that predates P5.4, `n_states == n` for every site, so
`r == n_ligands`, every offset table is the old one, and the state vector
layout is byte-identical. The full suite passed unchanged with the engine
edit in place and before `acetylcholine.py` existed, which is the check
that says so.

### Where the constants came from, and the two places they are weak

The nicotinic half is the strongest set of constants in this module and one
of the better-sourced in the codebase, because [Fenster1997] measured
activation potency, desensitization potency, desensitization onset and
recovery for FIVE subunit combinations in one experiment. That is the
[Volpe2011]/[Proudman2021]-style same-preparation guarantee P5.2 and P5.3
had to go looking for, and it means "alpha7 desensitizes 7.4-fold faster
and recovers 45.7-fold faster than alpha4beta2" is a comparison rather
than two quotations. The three subtypes this module does not build are kept in
`FENSTER1997_OTHER_SUBTYPES` for the same reason P5.3 kept alpha1B and
alpha1D: the 71-fold onset spread and 218-fold recovery spread across the
five rows are the scale against which the two modelled sites should be
read, and a test asserts both.

Two weaknesses, stated rather than smoothed:

**No measured association rate constant exists anywhere in this module.**
P5.1's derivation 3 says "share the site's measured `kon`". Here there is
no measured `kon` at any of the four sites for any of the four ligands, so
there is nothing to share, and `ILLUSTRATIVE_KON` is an explicitly
illustrative constant rather than a borrowed measurement. It is set to 0.01
nM^-1 min^-1 by two stated constraints rather than by taste: it sits at the
slow end of the only measured `kon` panel this codebase has ([Sykes2022] at
beta1, 0.00847 to 1.97 across 18 ligands, brought in by P5.3), so it does
not assert unusually fast binding; and it is fast enough that every site's
`koff` exceeds its `k_des` by at least 20-fold, so illustrative binding
never becomes the rate-limiting step in front of the measured gating
constants. A test asserts both. Every affinity is still exact, because
`koff = kon * Kd` by construction; only the approach timescale is hand-set.
[Sykes2009] measures precisely the missing quantity for acetylcholine at
M3 and is behind a Cloudflare-protected publisher site; it is named in the
module so the gap has an address.

**The muscarinic affinities are curated database values, not primary
measurements.** No single-laboratory M1-M5 panel carrying BOTH
acetylcholine and scopolamine was reachable: [Bolden1992] is the five-subtype
scopolamine panel and does not report acetylcholine; [Jakubik1997] is an
acetylcholine panel and stops at M4; [Wood1999] covers all five but uses
CARBACHOL as its reference full agonist, and substituting carbachol's
potency for acetylcholine's is exactly the ligand substitution rule 2
forbids. So the values come from the IUPHAR/BPS Guide to PHARMACOLOGY
release 2026.2, with every primary the Guide attributes each entry to named
in the module docstring, and the curated status labelled at the constant.
Where the Guide records a range, the module carries the pKi midpoint and
keeps both endpoints; the midpoint is labelled a derived number.

That range is not narrow. Acetylcholine's curated human pKi spans 4.3 to
6.5 across the five subtypes, a factor of 158, and 4.3 to 6.5 AT M2 ALONE.
This is P5.3's alpha2 affinity-state problem again: agonist binding to a
muscarinic receptor is biphasic and guanine-nucleotide-sensitive, so a
curated range over several laboratories brackets the G-protein-coupled
high-affinity state and the uncoupled low-affinity one at once. P5.3 could
build two selectable `AFFINITY_STATES` because it had a matched pair of
state-resolved measurements; here no such pair was reached, so the module
carries one midpoint per subtype and says what it is collapsing. The only
species check available, that the Guide's rat acetylcholine values (5.0,
6.4, 5.6 at M1-M3) fall inside the corresponding human ranges, is a test.

Scopolamine is in much better shape and the five-subtype table earns its
place by saying so: its pKi spans 8.7 to 9.4, a factor of 5 in Kd, so
"scopolamine blocks the muscarinic component" is subtype-independent in
this model in the way "prazosin blocks the alpha1 component" was in P5.3,
and it outbinds acetylcholine by more than 400-fold at every one of the
five. Both are tested.

### Derivation 4, which this task had to add

P5.1's three-way split assumes the literature reports equilibrium
affinities. The nicotinic literature does not. Every number available for
these receptors is a functional EC50 or IC50 from voltage clamp, because
these are ion channels and the assay that works on them measures current.
So a fourth case was needed and is stated at every constant that uses it:

> **4. A potency, not an affinity.** Use the functional EC50 as the site's
> conducting-state Kd, and say so.

The assumption is that activation is proportional to conducting-state
occupancy with no receptor reserve, which is precisely the assumption
`activation = sum(occupancy * efficacy)` already makes everywhere in this
codebase. It is the same limitation P5.2 flagged for the
530-fold-versus-31-fold D1/D2 gap and P5.3 for the 3.8-log-unit alpha1A
affinity/potency gap, applied here in the only direction the data allow.
For an ion channel with a Hill coefficient near 1 (1.1 for nicotine at
alpha7, 0.83 and 0.74 for acetylcholine at the two alpha4beta2
stoichiometries) it is a better approximation than it was for either
G-protein-coupled case, because there is no second-messenger amplification
step between occupancy and the measured signal.

### The prediction this makes, and gets wrong by tenfold

This is the part of P5.4 worth reading.

The Katz-Thesleff cycle has a consequence nobody put into it. Trapping
ligand in a desensitized state that cannot dissociate makes the site's
apparent equilibrium affinity for TOTAL binding tighter than its
conducting-state affinity by exactly

    1 + k_des / k_rec

Both rates are measured. So the factor is not a parameter, it is a
PREDICTION, and [Fenster1997] measured the thing it predicts, in the same
table: the gap between the activation EC50 and the desensitization IC50 of
the same receptor in the same experiment.

    site         1 + k_des/k_rec    EC50/IC50 measured    model / measured
    alpha4beta2       24.5                 246                1 / 10.0
    alpha7             4.8                  69                1 / 14.4

The model reproduces the direction at both sites, reproduces an order of
magnitude of the shift, and under-predicts it by 10 to 14-fold. That the
shortfall is in the same direction and within 1.4-fold of the same size at
two receptors whose measured rates differ 7.4-fold (`k_des`) and
45.7-fold (`k_rec`) is what makes it a finding rather than noise.

The mechanism [Fenster1997] itself names is the obvious candidate. Its
Table 2 reports that beta2-containing receptors need TWO components to
describe the decay (alpha4beta2: tau_slow 90.7 +/- 5.9 s, tau_fast
5.4 +/- 1.5 s, the fast one carrying 40.3 +/- 3.2% of the amplitude) and
concludes that "these data imply multiple desensitized states for these
receptors". `DesensitizingReceptorSite` has one desensitized state per
ligand and cannot hold two components. With a deeper, slower state that a
30-minute exposure reaches and a 4-minute fit does not, the true trapping
ratio is larger than the one a single-exponential fit reports, and the
model's factor is the single-exponential one.

No number was adjusted to close that gap, and the temptation to was real,
because it is one free constant away: setting `k_rec` to 1/8.9 min instead
of 1/86.9 min makes the factor come out at 246 exactly. It would also make
the receptor recover from desensitization in nine minutes rather than the
43 minutes [Fenster1999] measured and the 87 minutes [Fenster1997]
measured, i.e. it would trade a stated 10-fold error in one place for an
unstated 5 to 10-fold error in another, and it would destroy the module's
only independent check. Rule 5 says report the real error, and the real
error is a factor of 10 in one direction with a named mechanism behind it.
Two tests hold it: one asserts both factors, both shortfalls and,
separately, the DIRECTION (because the direction is the part that would
falsify the single-desensitized-state simplification if it flipped); the
other reaches the same 10.04 from the concentration axis, by showing the
model needs 10.04x the measured IC50 to half-desensitize the pool.

### The result that needs no comparison, because nothing else can produce it

One consequence of the third state is qualitative rather than quantitative,
and it is the clearest single statement of what P5.4 bought. Dose the
network with acetylcholine and wait ten minutes. `ACETYLCHOLINE_KE` clears
the transmitter with a half-life of eight seconds, so by then every
conducting occupancy and every competitive occupancy in the model has
returned to zero: the two muscarinic sites are empty, both nicotinic sites'
conducting fractions are below a thousandth, and the drug is gone.
alpha4beta2 is still an eighth desensitized. alpha7 is not.

That asymmetry is not a parameter. It is `ALPHA4BETA2_TAU_RECOVERY` (86.9
min) against `ALPHA7_TAU_RECOVERY` (1.9 min), two numbers from one table,
carried through the state vector. In a two-state model the receptor's state
is a function of the current concentration, so when the drug goes the
receptor is back, always, for both subtypes, and there is nowhere to put a
receptor that is unoccupied by any competitor and still unavailable. This
is what "cannot be represented by the existing two-state occupancy model"
means concretely, and it is a test and a printed line in the example rather
than an argument.

### How much the desensitization constants are actually worth

Less than four significant figures, and the module says so out loud.

    quantity          [Fenster1997]         [Fenster1999]
    desensitization   3.7 +/- 0.9 min       1.4 min (65%) / 17 min
                      (single exponential)  (biphasic)
    recovery          86.9 +/- 64.7 min     43 min

Same laboratory, same preparation, same receptor, two papers two years
apart. The recovery constants differ 2.0-fold and the 1997 value's own
standard error is 74% of its mean, so anything this module says about
recovery TIMING is good to about a factor of two and no better. The 1997
single-exponential onset of 3.7 min sits between the 1999 biphasic pair
(1.4 and 17 min), which is the most that can be said for it. All three are
carried as constants, the 1997 values are the defaults because they are the
ones measured in the same table as everything else here, and a test asserts
the 2.0-fold spread and the bracketing so neither can be forgotten.

### The circuit, and the rule that had to be re-checked rather than reused

Three nodes, and the same cortical loop P5.1 built and P5.3 reused, for
P5.3's reason: it is the same cortical microcircuit, and changing its
weights would imply a difference no source supports. A test asserts the two
loop weights and the cortical readout are literally equal across
`serotonin.py`, `noradrenaline.py` and `acetylcholine.py`.

    BF_Cholinergic   basal forebrain cholinergic neurons. Carries the M2
                     AUTORECEPTOR, identified in M2 knock-out mice rather
                     than by a selective drug ([Zhang2002]). No edges, for
                     P5.1's and P5.3's reason.
    PFC_Pyramidal    layer V/VI prefrontal pyramidal neurons. Carries
                     THREE acetylcholine receptors at once: M1 (Gq,
                     excitatory, [McCormick1986]), alpha4beta2 (cation
                     channel, excitatory, [Kassam2008]) and alpha7 (cation
                     channel, excitatory, [Alkondon1993]).
    PFC_GABA         local cortical interneurons, no receptor, present to
                     make the pyramidal node's response finite.

Rules 1 and 2 carry over unchanged and are re-asserted. Rule 3 is the one
that had to be re-checked: P5.3 established that the saturation budget is
per NODE rather than per receptor, and set two cortical gains to 0.5 each
because the node carried two receptors. This node carries three, so each
gets a third of the same unit. The counterfactual is re-run rather than
assumed: at P5.1's per-receptor unit rule the node would take +3.0 of
drive, and the test asserts that this pushes its sigmoid sensitivity below
`stability.SATURATION_FLOOR` while +1.0 does not. A rule that cannot reject
a value is not a rule, and this is the second task to test that it can.

Putting both nicotinic sites on ONE node with the SAME gain is deliberate,
and it is P5.3's device: every alpha7-versus-alpha4beta2 difference this
module reports is then a consequence of the published constants rather than
of two hand-set numbers.

### Searched and empty

- **Association rate constants**, for any of the four ligands at any of the
  four receptors. Covered above; `ILLUSTRATIVE_KON` and [Sykes2009] are the
  record of it.
- **A relative maximal response for nicotine against acetylcholine** at
  alpha4beta2 or alpha7 in one preparation. [ChavezNoriega1997] states only
  that acetylcholine was "one of the most efficacious agonists at all
  hnAChRs" except at h-alpha3beta2; [Fenster1997] normalizes to
  acetylcholine test pulses without reporting a ratio; the alpha7
  literature reached gives Imax relative to acetylcholine for nornicotine
  and for experimental partial agonists but not for nicotine itself.
  `NICOTINE_EFFICACY` is therefore 1.0 as a stated simplification. Nothing
  here depends on it, because both nicotinic results are about
  desensitization, which is driven by occupancy and not by efficacy, and a
  parameterized test re-runs them at 0.5.
- **A single-laboratory M1-M5 panel with both ligands.** Covered above.
- **Rodent PK for nicotine, scopolamine and mecamylamine.** Exists,
  extensively for nicotine, and not used, for P5.3's two unchanged reasons.
  All three share the one illustrative `TOOL_COMPOUND_KE` that
  `serotonin.py`, `dopamine.py` and `noradrenaline.py` share, and a test
  asserts the equality across all four modules.
- **Acetylcholine's own clearance rate.** The same gap the other three
  transmitters have and the most extreme case of it: acetylcholinesterase
  is one of the fastest enzymes known and works on a sub-millisecond
  timescale, so a literal rate would collapse an acetylcholine dose into a
  delta function far inside one integration step. `ACETYLCHOLINE_KE` is the
  same flagged 5.0 min^-1 proxy the other three modules use, and a test
  asserts that equality too. P6.2.

### What was deliberately not built

- **Voltage- and use-dependence of mecamylamine's block.** No membrane
  potential in this engine, and no channel-open state for "use" to be a
  function of.
- **The alpha4beta2 stoichiometry split.** [Sanders2022] measures
  acetylcholine EC50 at 1.6 uM for (alpha4)2(beta2)3 and 37.1 uM for
  (alpha4)3(beta2)2, and [Papke2013] measures mecamylamine at 18 uM and 2.4
  uM for the same two: the two stoichiometries differ 23-fold in one
  direction for the agonist and 7.5-fold in the OTHER direction for the
  blocker. Both are recorded as constants and both ratios are tested; the
  high-sensitivity form is instantiated because it is the one nanomolar
  nicotine engages and this module's headline result is about nanomolar
  nicotine. A receptor-assembly question is not a regional one, so no ISH
  map could settle it, exactly as P5.3 recorded for its subtype split.
- **The M3, M4 and M5 sites.** All five subtypes' constants are defined,
  because the task is a five-subtype one and because the cross-subtype
  comparison is the honest way to state how non-selective scopolamine is.
  They are not instantiated because this three-node circuit has no node
  whose identity would fix which of them it carries, and inventing a node
  to hold a receptor is the failure mode P5.2 recorded.
- **The basal forebrain to cortex edge.** P5.1's and P5.3's decision, and
  stronger here than in either: this module gives one cortical node THREE
  different acetylcholine receptors, so a signed weight would double-count
  the receptor layer three times over. P6.1.
- **Endogenous cholinergic tone.** Without it scopolamine and mecamylamine
  given alone are inert, and real scopolamine is famously not. The test
  that asserts inertness says it is a limitation and names P6.2 as the
  thing that should make it fail.
- **Nicotine's upregulation of alpha4beta2 receptor number.** Downstream of
  exactly the desensitized state this module now has ([Fenster1999] is a
  paper about that link) and operating over days. No receptor-number state
  and no such timescale here.

### What this task changes, and what it does not

- **One new module and one new receptor class**, plus the smallest engine
  change that could support it. `acetylcholine.py` and
  `DesensitizingReceptorSite` are new; `engine.py` gained `n_ligands`, a
  second offset table and `state_rows`; `ReceptorSite` gained an
  `n_states` attribute equal to `n`. `network.py`, `circuit.py`,
  `behavior.py`, `pk.py`, `scenarios.py`, `serotonin.py`, `dopamine.py` and
  `noradrenaline.py` are untouched.
- **Every existing test passes unchanged.** The engine edit was run against
  the full suite before `acetylcholine.py` existed (716 gate tests green
  with the new offsets and the new `n_states` in place and nothing using
  them), and the pre-P5.4 state vector layout is identical because
  `n_states == n` for every site that predates this task. None deleted,
  skipped, weakened or marked slow. 51 new test items, 17 of them on the
  mechanism alone with no pharmacology in them, all in the offline gate,
  which now runs 767 tests.
- **Ten instantiated ligand-site affinities are literature-sourced**, and
  constants are defined for all five muscarinic subtypes for both
  acetylcholine and scopolamine plus both alpha4beta2 stoichiometries for
  both acetylcholine and mecamylamine, across two receptor superfamilies
  and seven receptor subtypes. Four measured gating rate constants
  (`k_des` and `k_rec` at both nicotinic sites) drive the new state, and
  two further measured quantities (the two nicotine desensitization IC50s)
  are treated as prediction TARGETS rather than as inputs.
- **Two constants are illustrative and labelled and one of them is new in
  kind**: `ILLUSTRATIVE_KON` is the first parameter in this codebase where
  derivation 3 had nothing to borrow, so it is hand-set against two stated
  constraints instead, both tested.
- **A quantitative failure is reported rather than fitted away.** The
  10-fold and 14-fold shortfalls in the predicted apparent-affinity shift
  are the honest headline of P5.4, the mechanism behind them is named and
  cited, and the one-parameter change that would have hidden them is
  written down along with what it would have cost.
- **The circuit and the pharmacokinetics remain illustrative and labelled**,
  as in every scenario before Phase 7 - but rule 3's per-node budget has
  now been tested at three receptors on one node as well as at two, so a
  convention established by P5.3 has survived its first extension.

## Phase 5: glutamate NMDA and AMPA (P5.5)

### The task, and the question in it that is not about constants

The brief for P5.5 has three parts, and only the first is a sourcing
exercise:

> Add NMDA and AMPA receptors with cited constants for glutamate, ketamine,
> MK-801 and NBQX. NMDA voltage-dependent magnesium block and the fact that
> these receptors carry the fast excitatory transmission already implicit in
> the connectivity matrix both need explicit treatment: say clearly which
> role the connectivity weights already play, so glutamatergic transmission
> is not double-counted.

The second and third parts are the task. P5.4 asked a mechanism question
(is the existing receptor model the wrong size or the wrong shape?) and
answered it by adding a state. P5.5 asks a *bookkeeping* question, and the
honest answer turns out to remove a parameter rather than add one.

### The double count, stated precisely

`network.CircuitNetwork` integrates

    tau_i * dr_i/dt = -r_i + sigmoid(sum_j W[i,j] * r_j + drive_i)

Every receptor system from the mu-opioid scenario onward enters through
`drive_i`: the receptor activates, and `coupling[node] * activation` is
added to that node's input. That is the right shape for a neuromodulator.
It is the wrong shape for glutamate, because of what `W[i,j] > 0` already
means.

A positive entry of `W` is a net excitatory synaptic gain from population
`j` onto population `i`. In a mammalian forebrain those synapses are
glutamatergic and the receptors transducing them are AMPA and NMDA
receptors. This is not an interpretation P5.5 is imposing on the matrix; it
is the reading the matrix already had, in "Network layer: connectivity as a
signed matrix", in P3.2's derivation of excitatory/inhibitory sign from
region neurotransmitter identity, and in every hand-built cortical loop from
P5.1 onward, where the pyramidal-to-interneuron weight *is* the
glutamatergic projection.

So fast glutamatergic transmission was already in the model, at full
strength, in every simulation this codebase has ever run, before this
module existed. Adding an AMPA system with `coupling={"PFC_GABA": g}` would
have put the same synapse into the equations twice, as `W[i,j] * r_j` and
again as `g * activation`. Three things would then be wrong at once: the
drug-free fixed point would move for no physiological reason, the modelled
synapse would be roughly twice as strong as the connectome says, and an AMPA
antagonist could only ever remove one of the two copies, so a saturating
dose of NBQX would leave a full-strength glutamatergic synapse standing.

### The resolution, and the parameter it deletes

Glutamate receptor systems in `glutamate.py` have **empty `coupling`**, and
act only through `connection_modulation`:

    W_eff[i,j] = W[i,j] * (1 - share_NMDA * blocked_NMDA
                              - share_AMPA * blocked_AMPA)

The receptor layer's job for glutamate is not "how much drive does this
receptor deliver" - the circuit layer already answered that - but "what
fraction of the transmission already in `W[i,j]` do the drugs on board
remove". `share_NMDA + share_AMPA == 1` *partitions* the existing weight; it
does not add to it, and a test asserts the identity exactly rather than
approximately.

The consequence worth spelling out is that **P5.5 introduces no illustrative
coupling gain at all**, which no P5 module before it can say. P5.1 to P5.4
each had one hand-set `mechanism_gain` per receptor, each unidentifiable
from anything published (P2.3), each carried as a labelled illustrative
number. Here the corresponding quantity is pinned by algebra:
`1 + gain * activation` has to equal `1 - (fraction removed)`, so with
`activation` defined as the negative of the fraction removed, `gain == 1`
exactly. `GLUTAMATE_CONNECTION_GAIN` exists as a named constant only so that
the one place it could quietly become a tuning knob is visible, and a test
pins it.

That is the whole trade. The magnitude of glutamatergic transmission was
never this module's to set: it is `W[i,j]`, and it comes from the
connectome.

### Three honest costs of the resolution

1. **Exogenous glutamate cannot be an excitatory drug here.** Dosing the
   `glutamate` ligand raises occupancy at both sites and displaces a
   competitive antagonist - both real, both tested - but it cannot push
   transmission above `W[i,j]`, because `W[i,j]` already represents
   transmission with the endogenous transmitter present. Letting it would
   re-introduce exactly the double count. Endogenous transmitter tone as a
   first-class quantity is P6.2's job; until then this module's glutamate is
   a competitor at a binding site and nothing more.
2. **`baseline_input` is not modulated, and that under-states a systemic
   antagonist.** Each node's `baseline_input` stands in for everything
   outside the modelled loop, part of which is extrinsic glutamatergic
   afferents that a systemic NMDA antagonist would also reduce. P5.5
   deliberately does not scale it, because the term is of mixed and
   unlabelled origin and scaling it would assert a glutamatergic fraction of
   it that nothing measures. The model therefore under-states a systemic
   glutamate antagonist by whatever that fraction is. Stated once, asserted
   nowhere, because there is no number to assert.
3. **An antagonist alone is no longer inert, and this is a break with every
   earlier module.** P5.1 to P5.4 each had to record that their antagonists
   do nothing without endogenous transmitter tone, because there was no
   agonist for them to displace. Glutamate antagonists in P5.5 are not
   inert: the transmission they remove is already in the connectivity
   weight, so it does not need a dose to exist. That is a direct consequence
   of the resolution above and it is the first time this codebase can model
   an antagonist given alone the way pharmacology actually gives one. A test
   states it in exactly those terms.

### The magnesium block, and the membrane potential this model does not have

An NMDA receptor's conductance is blocked by extracellular Mg2+ in a
voltage-dependent way ([Nowak1984], [Mayer1984]). This is what makes the
receptor a coincidence detector, and it is why NMDA-mediated transmission
is not a fixed conductance but a function of the postsynaptic state.

This codebase's circuit layer is a population-rate model. It has no membrane
potential, in any node, at any time. There is no way to make the block
dynamic here without first inventing a rate-to-voltage map, and no
measurement of "the mean membrane potential of a cortical population firing
at half its maximum rate" exists to anchor one, because that is a property
of this model rather than of any preparation (see the searched-and-empty
record in `glutamate.py`).

The split P5.5 makes is between the two halves of that problem:

- **The block itself is measured and implemented exactly.**
  `mg_unblocked_fraction(V)` is [ChiuCarter2022]'s conductance-voltage fit -
  mouse, acute cortical slice, 34.7 C, junction-potential corrected, three
  physiological ionic conditions, fitted over -78 to +32 mV. Nothing in that
  function is hand-set, and tests check that each fit reproduces its own
  published midpoint, that the three conditions order correctly by their
  Mg2+, and that the function is monotone across the fitted range.
- **The voltage it is evaluated at is one labelled illustrative constant.**
  `ILLUSTRATIVE_OPERATING_VOLTAGE = -40 mV`, chosen as a round value inside
  the measured range and well depolarized from rest because this codebase's
  nodes sit at half their maximum firing rate at baseline. It is not a
  measured membrane potential of anything. Every headline result is swept
  across the measured range rather than asserted at that point.

[JahrStevens1990]'s canonical form, `1/(1 + [Mg2+]/3.57 * exp(-0.062 V))`,
is recorded and not used, and the reason is specific: the primary is behind
a publisher block that returned HTTP 403 to every retrieval attempt, so its
two constants could not be checked against the paper that is supposed to
contain them. This module does not put unverifiable numbers in its equations
when a verifiable, same-species, physiological-temperature alternative is in
hand. `jahr_stevens_unblocked_fraction` exists so the two can be compared,
and a test reports the comparison: in 1 mM Mg2+ the canonical form is the
*deeper* block, by 1.2-fold at -60 mV and 1.4-fold at -40 mV, so substituting
it would shrink every NMDA effect in this module without changing a sign.

Doing the block exactly immediately constrains the whole module. At the
resting potential [ChiuCarter2022] measured in the same cells (-82.7 mV in
their awake ionic condition) the block removes 97% of the NMDA conductance,
so NMDA's share of an excitatory weight there is 0.8% and an NMDA antagonist
can do essentially nothing. Ketamine's leverage on this circuit is a
27-fold monotone function of the operating potential, over the measured
range, entirely from the measured fit. That is the module's most
load-bearing prediction and it has its own test.

### How the two measurements compose without either being counted twice

    share_NMDA(V) = R * b(V) / (1 + R * b(V))

where `b(V)` is the measured unblocked fraction and `R` is the NMDA:AMPA
conductance ratio *with the block removed*. The choice of `R` is the reason
[Myme2003] is the source rather than any of the many papers reporting an
NMDA:AMPA ratio: [Myme2003] isolated its mixed mEPSCs in **nominally zero
Mg2+**, which is exactly the Mg2+-free ratio this composition needs. Taking
a ratio measured in physiological Mg2+ and then applying a Mg2+ block to it
would have been a second, subtler double count, of the same kind as the one
this whole section is about.

`R = 0.27` (rat medial PFC layer 2/3, n = 27; the visual-cortex value in the
same paper is 0.28). Its known error is directional and stated rather than
corrected: it is a *peak-current* ratio, and [Myme2003] measured the NMDA
component's decay at 69 ms while an AMPA EPSC decays in a few ms, so the
share of transmitted *charge* - which is what a rate model integrates - is
larger than 0.27. The same paper notes that evoked EPSCs in 2 mM Mg2+ at
depolarized potentials gave a larger ratio still. Both point the same way,
so P5.5 records that `R` is a lower bound and does not adjust it, because
the matching AMPA decay constant was not retrievable and a correction
factor would have been invented.

### Two antagonists, two mechanisms, and why that is not a stylistic choice

- **NBQX is competitive**, and this is a measurement rather than an
  assumption: [Randle1992]'s Schild analysis gives pA2 7.05 +/- 0.10 against
  AMPA with slopes near unity. So NBQX gets an ordinary orthosteric ligand
  entry in the same competitive pool as glutamate, and needs nothing
  `ReceptorSite` did not already do - the same finding P5.1 recorded for
  diazepam/flumazenil and P5.4 for scopolamine.
- **Ketamine and MK-801 are uncompetitive open-channel blockers**
  ([Huettner1988]: "binding and unbinding of MK-801 seems to be possible
  only if the N-Me-D-Asp-operated channel is in the transmitter-activated
  state"). Putting them in the competitive pool would assert that they
  displace glutamate, which is the one thing they demonstrably do not do.
  They get an independent pool that scales transmission multiplicatively.

This is P5.4's mecamylamine argument again, and it is reused rather than
re-derived: `receptor.py` gains `ChannelBlockingReceptorSite`, which is
`DesensitizingReceptorSite` minus the desensitized states, so that the
channel-block mechanism is available without dragging in a gating cycle that
