independent readings rather than one reading against itself. Both mutations now
fail it. Anything that pins a derived value has to be derived a second, different
way or it pins nothing.

The inference the convention makes - that a region's contribution is monotone in
its population rate - is exactly what a linear readout means, and it is wrong in
at least three documented cases. Those are handled below rather than hidden.

### `contested`: the flag, and the rule that keeps it from swallowing everything

The first draft of this module flagged a term contested whenever a paper reported
cell-type heterogeneity. That flags everything: every region has subpopulations
that differ, and a flag that fires on all 69 terms carries no information. The
rule that actually discriminates is narrower:

> `contested=True` when TWO studies manipulating this REGION report opposite
> directions for THIS endpoint. Subpopulation heterogeneity alone is not enough;
> it goes in `note`.

A contested term is recorded in full, excluded from the default readout, and
returned by `resolve(..., include_contested=True)`, so what it is worth is
measurable rather than asserted. Sixteen of the 69 terms are contested, and the
distribution is itself a finding:

    endpoint              terms  contested  what contests them
    locomotion              11      3       CP, GPe: two intermingled populations
                                            with opposite locomotor signs inside
                                            one CCF structure. STN: bulk
                                            inhibition is pro-locomotor
                                            ([Guillaumin2021]) and brief lateral
                                            inhibition is anti-locomotor
                                            ([Callahan2024]).
    anxiety                 12      6       BLA, BST, CEA, PL, ILA, ZI - amygdala,
                                            BNST, mPFC and zona incerta each
                                            contain opposite-signed populations,
                                            and four of the six are contested by
                                            a paper contesting ITSELF.
    analgesia               11      1       RM, and it is the important one.
    reward                  11      0       Not agreement: the disagreements here
                                            are between subpopulations rather
                                            than between two studies of the
                                            region, so they sit in `note`.
    sedation                 9      1       DR: [Oikonomou2019]'s serotonergic
                                            raphe promotes SLEEP, [Cho2017]'s
                                            raphe dopamine neurons promote WAKE,
                                            same voxels.
    working_memory           6      0
    sensorimotor_gating      9      5       The highest fraction, for reasons
                                            specific to the assay (below).

Anxiety and prepulse inhibition are the two endpoints whose default readouts are
thinnest (6 and 4 active terms). That is the literature, reported rather than
padded.

### Three regions where a linear readout is provably wrong, and one of them is a gift to P7.2

P7.2 is "nonlinear decoder, only where data supports one over the linear
readout". P7.1 hands it three concrete cases rather than a vague warrant:

1. **RM / rostral ventromedial medulla, in analgesia.** [ZhuoGebhart1997], rat,
   tail flick: at 43 of 86 RVM sites, low-intensity stimulation (5-25 uA)
   FACILITATED the tail-flick reflex and higher intensity (50-200 uA) INHIBITED
   it, reproduced by 5 nmol against 50 nmol glutamate *at the same sites*. One
   region, one paper, one assay, and the effect reverses with the region's own
   drive. No linear weight can be right for it.
2. **ACB and ventral CA1/SUB, in prepulse inhibition.** Both hyperactivation
   ([Wang2015], [Swerdlow1990]) and inactivation ([Zhang2002], [Kodsi1994]) lower
   gating - an inverted U. The signs recorded capture the hyperactivation limb,
   which is the limb drugs move, and both terms are contested.
3. **Working memory, structurally.** All six terms are positive and no negatively
   signed region was found - see the searched-and-empty record. The consequence,
   stated on the endpoint: this readout is, up to scale, the mean rate over six
   regions, so any drug that shifts global excitability moves it with no
   circuit-specific effect at all. The inverted-U that prefrontal dopamine is
   famous for is precisely the shape an all-positive linear readout cannot hold.

### Resolution: an endpoint does not know what parcellation it will be read at

`connectome/build.py` builds at 291, 60 or 12 nodes, and the same seven endpoints
have to work at all three. A term names CCF structures; `resolve()` maps each
onto whichever node the network has, by four rules, and reports which fired:

    exact        the structure IS a node                    full term weight
    ancestor     the nearest ancestor is a node             full term weight
    descendants  the nodes below it are                     weight SPLIT
    unmapped     none of the above                          dropped, and named

Rule 3's split is arithmetic and not convenience: a parent's mean rate is the
volume-weighted mean of its children's, so `w * r_parent = sum_i (w v_i / V) r_i`.
`region_sizes` supplies the `v_i` (voxel counts are the natural choice); without
them the equal split is an extra illustrative assumption and is reported as
`illustrative-equal-split` rather than passed off as exact.

**Two collapse rules, and why the default is the mean.** At coarse parcellations
several terms land on one node. `collapse="mean"` stops an endpoint silently
reweighting itself towards whichever region the CCF happens to subdivide most
finely; `collapse="sum"` is the other defensible reading (each experiment is
independent evidence) and the tests run both.

**The bug that rule exposed, and the fix.** A term may itself name several
structures - the reward endpoint's hippocampal term is [Meyers2006]'s dorsal
hippocampus, which is CA1 + CA3 + DG. Under a naive implementation that term
would give the hippocampus three units against BLA's one purely because the CCF
subdivides it. So a term's weight is split 1/N across its own structures, and
those structures SUM back within the term before the mean/sum choice is applied
ACROSS terms. Get that order wrong in either direction and one of two tests
fails: `test_a_term_is_one_unit_of_evidence_however_many_structures_it_names`
(fine parcellation, hippocampus must equal BLA) or
`test_the_same_term_collapsed_onto_one_node_keeps_its_full_weight` (coarse
parcellation, HPF must still equal BLA).

**Sign cancellation is reported, not smoothed.** When terms of opposite sign land
on one node they cancel under either rule, and `ResolvedEndpoint.cancellations`
names every node where it happened. That is the parcellation saying it cannot
express the endpoint. The clearest case is locomotion at 12 nodes: SNr, CUN, PPN,
SNc and VTA all become MB and SNr's sign is opposite to the other four, so MB
arrives at 3/5 of what it should be and the report says so. `results/
behavioral_endpoints.txt` shows this for all seven endpoints at all three
resolutions; a division-level whole-brain run should be read with it open.

### Normalisation, and what a score means before P7.3

After resolution the weights are scaled so `sum_i |w_i| == 1`. A Wilson-Cowan
rate is in [0, 1], so a normalised score is in [-1, 1] and the seven endpoints
are on one scale. Normalising AFTER resolution means a dropped term does not
shrink the score of the terms that survived. The resting score is
`0.5 * sum_i w_i` and is NOT zero - it is zero only for an endpoint whose signs
happen to balance - so what a drug does is `delta()`, the difference from the
drug-free run. Nothing here converts a score into seconds of tail-flick latency
or centimetres travelled; that is P7.3 and it is the reason `delta` and not
`score` is the quantity the example prints.

### The one place the evidence forced a structural decision: analgesia is two assays

The brief names analgesia once, with "(tail-flick, hot plate)" as its assays. The
literature says those are not one endpoint. **Two** papers ran BOTH assays in one
preparation and found them to dissociate, in opposite manipulation directions:

    [Pastoriza1996]  rat, medial frontal lesion: HOT PLATE latency +82%,
                     TAIL FLICK unchanged
    [Hao2025]        mouse, retrosplenial-to-cingulate activation: thermal
                     responses facilitated, "did not influence spinal
                     nociceptive responses in the tail-flick test"

Two more dissociate tail flick from a *different* supraspinal measure without
running hot plate, which supports the same spinal/supraspinal split without being
evidence about hot plate: [Roberts1994] (submedial thalamic lesion: vocalization
threshold down, tail flick unchanged) and [MorganFranklin1990] (VTA 6-OHDA:
formalin analgesia abolished, tail flick "completely unchanged").

**This paragraph first claimed six papers and is worth leaving the correction in.**
The draft added [Xie2023] and [Samineni2017] as "supraspinal-only effects", and
neither ran either assay - this module's own citation entry for [Samineni2017]
says "Assay is Hargreaves and von Frey, NOT tail-flick or hot plate" verbatim,
and Hargreaves is a spinally-mediated withdrawal latency, so the characterisation
was wrong twice over. Padding the count of a structural decision's justification
with papers that did not measure the thing is the same category error as
substituting one assay for another; it was caught by an adversarial review of the
module and not by the tests, which is itself worth knowing.

One shared weight vector is contradicted by [Pastoriza1996] and [Hao2025]
directly. Averaging over them would be exactly the substitution rule 2 of this
codebase forbids. So the module keeps
the union endpoint the roadmap asks for - `ENDPOINTS` has seven members and a
test asserts it - and publishes `ASSAY_VARIANTS`, two restrictions of it built by
`Endpoint.restrict_to_assay`. They are views, not an eighth endpoint: every term
in them is a term of `analgesia`, which a test asserts too. They select genuinely
different regions:

    analgesia_tail_flick   CEA, LC, SMT, ZI   (+ RM, contested)
    analgesia_hot_plate    ACAd, DR, PAG

Only the supraspinal assay reaches the cingulate; only the spinal one reaches the
submedial thalamus. That is [Pastoriza1996]'s dissociation, as a property of the
object rather than as a remark.

**Why `assay` is a controlled vocabulary and not prose.** The first
implementation matched the restriction as a substring of a free-text assay field,
and it was wrong in a way worth recording because the failure mode is
instructive: ACAd's assay read `"hot plate (tail flick explicitly unchanged)"`,
so restricting to tail flick pulled in the one term that most sharply does NOT
belong there, with its sign intact. Negations do not survive substring matching.
`assays` is now a tuple of tokens matched by exact membership, caveats live in
`note`, and `test_restrict_to_assay_matches_tokens_exactly_not_as_a_substring`
pins the case that broke.

### The CCF, and six ways it does not fit this literature

Every acronym was checked against P3.1's structure graph, and a full-cache test
asserts something stronger than existence: that every acronym is a *row* of the
Knox 291-region set, so nothing is silently lost at `resolution="regions"`. All
of them are. Getting there required four substitutions and cost two omissions:

    ventral pallidum -> SI + MA     There is no "VP" acronym. PALv exists in the
                                    ontology but is not a Knox row.
    RVM              -> RM          [Urban1994] shows the effective tissue spans
                                    RM plus medial GRN plus PGRNl, so the RM
                                    term is narrower than the papers behind it.
    SLEAc            -> named only  [Sun2023]'s target is not in the CCF at all.
                                    Named on the term, not substituted.
    MLR              -> CUN + PPN   Not a CCF structure; two separate terms.
    RMTg             -> dropped     Not a CCF structure.
    stop cells       -> dropped     [Capelli2017]/[Bouvier2015]'s arrest
                                    population does not map onto one region.

Two CCF traps are recorded because either one would silently invert a whole node,
and both were live risks in this task:

* **`LH` is the LATERAL HABENULA** (parent EPI). The lateral hypothalamus is
  `LHA`. Both appear in the reward endpoint **with opposite signs**.
* **`PPT` is the POSTERIOR PRETECTAL nucleus.** The pedunculopontine tegmental
  nucleus is `PPN`, and `PPN` carries terms in three of the seven endpoints.

And two structural limits the parcellation imposes, which no amount of care
removes:

* **`ACB` has no children in the CCF**, so the core/shell dissociation that most
  of the place-preference literature turns on cannot be represented. One study
  dissociates two of this module's own endpoints *inside* the nucleus in a single
  experiment - core to locomotion, medial shell to place preference - and a
  single ACB node averages over them.
* **`CP` contains two intermingled, roughly equinumerous populations with
  opposite locomotor signs** ([Kravitz2010]), so a scalar CP rate has no
  defensible sign at all. Recorded contested and excluded by default. A
  locomotion readout without the dorsal striatum is a strange object, and it is
  the honest one.

### Species, stated once and never adjusted

The roadmap fixes the species at mouse. Sedation is 9 of 9 mouse; working memory
is mouse for the prefrontal, mediodorsal and hippocampal terms and rat for
reuniens and medial septum; locomotion is 11 of 11 mouse; reward is 6 mouse to
5 rat; **analgesia is
rat-dominated (9 of 11) and sensorimotor gating is 8 of 9 rat**. That is not laziness: the
tail-flick and hot-plate causal literature is 1980s-2010s rat microinjection
pharmacology, and the modern mouse circuit work migrated to Hargreaves and von
Frey. Every term carries its own `species`, a test asserts that rat terms still
exist (a library in which every species had quietly become mouse is the failure
rule 2 exists to prevent), and no term's species was changed to match the model.

### Searched and empty

`endpoints.SEARCHED_AND_EMPTY` is the full record; the shape of it is worth
summarising here because two entries change what the module can claim.

**Regions with no usable evidence for an endpoint they obviously belong in.**
`MOp`/`MOs` carry no locomotion weight (every query returned neurotoxicology,
stroke or corticospinal-plasticity papers with no ambulation-linked causal
manipulation). `SSp` and the insular areas carry no analgesia weight - the one
strong causal mouse S1 paper uses von Frey MECHANICAL testing only, and rule 2
forbids substituting it for a thermal latency. `CEA` carries no reward weight,
`ACB` and the basal forebrain no working-memory weight, `DG` and `SUB` no
working-memory weight (no structure-selective causal study exists; every hit was
a whole-hippocampus or fimbria-fornix manipulation), `CUN` no sedation weight.
`GRN` and `PRNr` are dropped from prepulse inhibition on [Davis1982]'s own
negative controls.

**Every weight in this module comes from a causal manipulation and none from an
imaging prior**, and that is not a preference. Separate sweeps for a brain-wide
c-Fos or light-sheet activation map of elevated-plus-maze open-arm exposure, of
hot plate or tail flick, and of psychostimulant hyperlocomotion or place
preference all came back empty of anything on-point. The brief offers "lesion or
imaging evidence"; only the first half of that was available. `EndpointTerm`
still accepts `technique="imaging"` and `ResolvedEndpoint.report()` still counts
correlative terms separately - the machinery is there, unused, because the
literature is.

**Two measured nulls, which are stronger than absences.** VTA carries no
analgesia weight because [MorganFranklin1990] measured its absence: bilateral
6-OHDA of the ventral tegmentum abolished morphine analgesia in the formalin test
and left tail-flick analgesia "completely unchanged". And there is no paper
showing chemogenetic Gq excitation of VTA dopamine neurons produces place
preference; all sufficiency evidence for that is optogenetic, and the one
Gi-DREADD study reported a null on cocaine CPP while still reducing the drug's
locomotor effect.

### What this module deliberately does not do

* **It does not fit anything.** No magnitude here is calibrated. P7.3.
* **It does not convert a score into an assay unit.** P7.3.
* **It does not introduce a nonlinearity**, though it names three places one is
  needed. P7.2.
* **It does not touch `behavior.BehaviorReadout`, `scenarios.py` or any Phase 5
  module.** `Endpoint.resolve()` returns a plain `BehaviorReadout`, which a test
  asserts by `type(...) is`, so everything downstream that already scores one
  keeps working. This is P3.2's promise about `CircuitNetwork` and P6.1's about
  the hand-built scenarios, made a third time.
* **It does not read out the hand-built scenarios.** Their nodes are populations
  ("VTA_DA"), not CCF regions, and `resolve` ignores any node name the ontology
  cannot resolve - which a test pins, because silently matching "VTA_DA" to VTA
  would be worse than dropping it.

### What an adversarial review of the finished module found

The module was reviewed against its own docstrings before commit, with the
instruction to check every sign against its prose and to look for tests that
would pass if the thing they claim to check were broken. It found no sign error
in the 69 terms. It found five things worth fixing, all of which are fixed
above and none of which was caught by the tests as first written:

1. **The sign test was tautological** (above). The most valuable finding, because
   the module's central claim rested on it.
2. **The justification for `ASSAY_VARIANTS` claimed six papers and had two**
   (above). Padding the count with papers that ran neither assay.
3. **Three internal counts contradicted the data**: the sedation notes said
   "eight of nine negative, VLPO the only positive one" when the contested `DR`
   term is also positive (7 negative, 2 positive); the analgesia notes said two
   off-assay terms when there are three (`GRN`, `PB`, `MD`); the working-memory
   notes said "the mean rate over six regions" for six TERMS over seven regions.
4. **A false-positive in the cancellation report.** `{1 if p > 0 else -1}`
   classified a zero part as negative, so two SAME-signed terms reaching one node
   through a zero-size descendant split were reported as cancelling. A false
   positive in the module's own honesty mechanism is worse than a silent failure.
5. **Partial `region_sizes` silently collapsed a term.**
   `region_sizes.get(d, 0.0)` gave the covered descendants the whole term weight
   and the missing ones nothing, while `split_was_equal` stayed False so the
   report claimed a volume-weighted split. The natural caller passes voxel counts
   from a build, which need not cover every node. Rule 3 now requires a positive
   size for EVERY descendant and falls back to the equal split otherwise.

Two smaller ones are also fixed: the report counted causal terms over the terms
OFFERED rather than the terms that LANDED (so "8 causal terms" could sit next to
four nodes), and five bracketed citations in the prose - [Freeze2013],
[PadillaCoreano2016], [Parfitt2017], [Gao2023], [Bouvier2015] - resolved to
nothing, because the orphan-citation test only checked one of the two directions
its docstring claimed. All five were added to `CITATIONS` rather than deleted
from the prose, since each bounds or contests a sign.

### `inferred`: the eight terms whose direction was reasoned, not measured

The review's sharpest structural point was that `activity` and `measure` are
presented as readings off an experiment, and for eight of the 69 terms at least
one of them is an argument. That is now a field rather than a caveat buried in
prose, counted by `ResolvedEndpoint.report()` and printed by
`Endpoint.summary()`:

    anxiety   SUB   the manipulation was at AHN, one synapse downstream
    gating    PRNc  the cited experiment measured startle amplitude; the
                    `measure` comes from the argument that gating IS
                    inhibition of this nucleus
    analgesia PAG   opioid raises vlPAG output only via disinhibition
    analgesia DR    the same disinhibition step
    gating    PL/ILA a D1 agonist is read as raising cortical activity
    gating    ACB   dopamine in the accumbens has NO unambiguous direction:
                    it excites D1- and inhibits D2-expressing neurons
    analgesia PB    the assay is defensive responding, so `measure` is a
                    translation into withdrawal latency
    analgesia MD    the assay is place aversion, same translation

Five of the eight are already contested or off-assay, so the flag mostly marks
terms a reader was already being told to discount. The two that it newly exposes
are analgesia `PAG` and `DR`, which are among the endpoint's strongest terms by
citation quality and rest on an inference the module had stated only in prose.

### What P7.1 delivered, checked against the standing discipline

- **Seven endpoints, each a multi-region readout**, resolving onto the real
  291-region connectome network at all three resolutions with nothing unmapped.
  Region counts at full resolution: locomotion 8, anxiety 6, analgesia 10,
  reward 14, sedation 11, working memory 7, sensorimotor gating 5 (default,
  contested excluded).
- **69 cited terms across 7 endpoints**, every one carrying its citation,
  species, technique, assay and the finding written out so the sign can be
  checked against the experiment rather than trusted - and, for the eight where
  the direction had to be reasoned, an `inferred` field saying what was reasoned.
- **108 citations, every author list, title and journal reference taken
  VERBATIM from PubMed's own esummary record for the PMID.** This was not the
  first plan and the reason for it is worth recording, because it is the
  closest this task came to breaking rule 1. Drafting the citations by hand
  from the literature sweep produced sixteen entries whose title did not match
  the PMID and, worse, more than a dozen whose author list past the first
  author was **wrong or invented** - [Sun2023] was attributed to a nine-author
  Chinese group when the paper is Sun, Qian, Xu, Hunt and Sah; [Li1998] gained
  a co-author it does not have; [Shah2025] gained six. None of that changes a
  number, and all of it is fabrication of exactly the kind the standing
  discipline forbids. The fix was mechanical rather than careful: every
  citation's bibliographic prefix is now regenerated from the live record and
  only the commentary after `PMID:nnnn.` is written here. A checker confirms
  that all 107 entries with a PMID start with PubMed's author string and
  contain PubMed's title. `scripts/verify_pmids.py` is committed with the
  module so the check can be re-run.
- **Every weight labelled illustrative**, enforced two ways: the endpoint
  declares `weights_are_illustrative` and `EndpointTerm` has no magnitude
  attribute at all, so there is nothing for a fitted number to quietly become.
- **The signs derived rather than asserted**, and re-derived by a test.
- **Sixteen contested terms recorded, excluded by default, and measurable**, with
  a rule that stops the flag from swallowing every term.
- **Three named targets for P7.2**, one of them ([ZhuoGebhart1997]) a
  within-paper, within-assay, within-site reversal that no linear weight can fit.
- **The analgesia assay dissociation made structural**, with the substring bug
  that motivated the controlled vocabulary recorded rather than quietly fixed.
- **A searched-and-empty record with eleven region-endpoint gaps, four CCF
  substitutions, two CCF traps, two structural limits and two measured nulls.**
- **Tests.** A new `tests/test_endpoints.py` (38 items, 4 of them
  `full_data_only`). None slow, none skipped when the cache is present. No
  existing test changed, because nothing existing moved. Two of the 38 pin bugs
  the review found in the resolver, and both were mutation-tested by reverting
  the fix and watching them fail; so was `EXPECTED_SIGNS`, against two
  independent term flips.
- **Outputs**: `examples/behavioral_endpoint_library.py` and
  `scripts/report_endpoints.py` -> `results/behavioral_endpoints.txt`.
## Phase 7: a nonlinear decoder, only where held-out data says so (P7.2)

### The sentence in the brief, and the question it does not answer

> Evaluate whether a nonlinear decoder outperforms the linear readout for
> each endpoint, using held-out data and a model comparison criterion. Adopt
> nonlinearity only where it wins on held-out data.

The criterion is specified and the discipline is specified. What is not
specified, and what turned out to be the whole task, is WHICH held-out data.
A decoder is the map from regional firing rates to a behavioural score, so
the data that can compare two decoders has to pair ACTIVITY with BEHAVIOUR.
There are two candidate sources in reach and only one of them is admissible.

**Drug dose-response curves are not admissible, and this is not a close
call.** They are the obvious choice - the brief's own sentence "behavioral
endpoints are frequently saturating or non-monotonic in dose" points
straight at them - and they are what P7.3 exists to fit. But a drug moves
every region at once, through pharmacokinetics, then competitive binding,
then a recurrent Wilson-Cowan network, and only then through the decoder. A
dose-response curve is curved for reasons living in four layers. Fitting a
nonlinear decoder to one and declaring the decoder nonlinear because it fit
better assigns all four layers' curvature to the fourth. Worse, it would do
so BEFORE P7.3 has fitted the other three, so the decoder would absorb
whatever the uncalibrated layers got wrong and then be frozen there. That is
the sequencing reason P7.2 precedes P7.3 rather than the reverse, and it is
worth stating because the natural reading of the brief is the opposite.

**Graded single-region manipulations are admissible.** Set one region's
drive to several levels - stimulation intensity, optogenetic frequency,
intracerebral dose - and measure the behaviour at each. That is a direct
observation of the decoder along one coordinate, with the pharmacokinetic
and binding layers absent by construction.

### The asymmetry that makes the comparison possible at all

Let `u` be the drive, `r(u)` the region's rate, `b` the behaviour. Under a
linear decoder, holding the other regions fixed,

    b(u) = const + w r(u)

`r(u)` is unknown. One thing about it is not: it is MONOTONE and SATURATING.
More current, more light, more agonist does not reverse the direction in
which it pushes the region, and a Wilson-Cowan unit's output is a bounded
sigmoid of its input. Monotone DECREASING counts, and has to: driving an
inhibitory input harder lowers the target's rate monotonically, which is
[DeLuca2022]'s orexin terminals in the VLPO below, and an affine map of a
monotone-decreasing function is still monotone. The first draft of this
argument said "monotone non-decreasing" and would have excluded that series
for no reason. Two consequences follow and they are not symmetric.

**A saturating `b(u)` says nothing about the decoder.** If behaviour bends
over as drive rises, `r(u)` bending over explains it completely with a linear
`w`. Adopting a saturating decoder here would attribute the sigmoid the
circuit layer ALREADY HAS to the readout and count it twice. This is the
commonest shape in the graded literature, so the rule has to reject it
explicitly rather than let a model comparison find it "better".

**A non-monotone `b(u)` cannot come from a linear decoder.** A monotone
non-decreasing `r(u)` composed with an affine map is monotone for every `w`.
So a behaviour that rises and then falls as ONE region's drive is raised is
inconsistent with a linear readout over that region's rate, and no choice of
weight repairs it.

So the comparison this module runs is not "linear versus curved", which the
transduction confounds beyond identification. It is "monotone versus
non-monotone", which it does not. Every design decision below follows from
that sentence.

### Four families, two of which are the actual comparison

Over a drive coordinate `z` rescaled to `[0, 1]` across each series' own
levels:

    constant     a                          1 parameter   the null
    linear       a + b z                    2             nested in both
    satexp       a + c (1 - exp(-lam z))    3             monotone, saturating
    quadratic    a + b z + c z^2            3             the only non-monotone one

`satexp` and `quadratic` carry the SAME parameter count over the SAME
predictor. That is deliberate: if the two sides of the head-to-head differed
in complexity, a verdict would be partly about complexity rather than about
shape. `constant` is there so that "this series carries no signal" is a
verdict the machinery can reach rather than a case that silently falls
through to whichever family fits noise best.

The criterion is leave-one-out cross-validation: hold out one drive level,
refit, predict it, and root-mean-square the held-out errors. AICc is computed
and printed as a second, in-sample criterion, and it deliberately does NOT
gate the verdict: at four or five drive levels, AICc for a 3-parameter family
is either undefined (`n - k - 1 <= 0`) or dominated by its own small-sample
correction. Reporting a number whose correction term exceeds the quantity
being corrected, and then deciding on it, would be worse than not having it.

### The adoption rule, and the rule that had to be added after it failed

    ADOPT for a series iff ALL of
      1. at least 4 drive levels;
      2. `quadratic` has the strictly lowest leave-one-out RMSE of the four;
      3. `quadratic` beats `constant` (the series has signal at all);
      4. the fitted turning point z* = -b/(2c) lies strictly inside (0, 1);
      5. the MEASURED MEANS are ordinally non-monotone;
      6. rules 2-5 hold under BOTH weightings of the levels.

Rules 1-4 were the design. Rule 5 was added because rule 4 turned out not to
be enough, and the case that broke it is kept in the test suite rather than
described:

    levels  0   1    2    3    4    5
    means   0   3.0  5.2  6.6  7.4  7.7

That is strictly increasing and decelerating - the canonical saturating
shape, the shape the argument above says carries NO decoder information.
`quadratic` beats `satexp` out of sample on it, and its vertex sits at
`z* = 0.945`, INSIDE the tested range. Rules 2, 3 and 4 all pass and the
series was adopted. That is precisely the false positive this module exists
to prevent, produced by the module's own rule, on its second test.

The reason is structural rather than accidental: a parabola fitted to a
saturating curve puts its stationary point wherever the curve flattens, and
on a saturating curve that is near the top of the sampled range. Rule 4 only
catches the version where the flattening happens past the last level.

Rule 5 is the fix and it is deliberately model-free: if the published means
never turn round, no reversal was measured, whatever a fitted parabola's
stationary point does. It reads the same claim a second, independent way
instead of trusting one reading of it, which is the discipline that replaced
P7.1's tautological sign test. It can only ever REMOVE adoptions, so it
cannot manufacture a nonlinearity; the cost is that a genuine reversal whose
last level lands a hair the wrong side of its predecessor is rejected. That
is the safe direction and it is stated on the rule.

`test_a_saturating_series_whose_vertex_falls_just_inside_is_still_rejected`
holds those six numbers, and deleting the `observed_shape` check turns it
red.

Rule 6 was added later still, and for the same kind of reason: rules 2-5 all
passed on real data, on a difference of 0.06 cm/s between two levels that
evoke no behaviour at all. Every series is therefore assessed twice, once
with the levels weighted equally and once by `1/SEM^2` from the published
dispersion, and a nonlinearity is adopted only if both agree. Neither
weighting is right on its own - `1/SEM^2` is the textbook choice and is
actively misleading where a low level sits on a floor, uniform discards
genuine precision - so requiring agreement is the way to make no adoption
depend on the choice, and it introduces no constant to tune. The series that
forced it is [Herent2023] and it is worked through below.

### No tuned number anywhere in the rule

There is no minimum effect size, no p-value, no margin by which `quadratic`
must beat the monotone families, and no smoothing. The rule is a strict
inequality on a held-out criterion, a structural constraint on where the
turning point sits, a model-free look at the means, and agreement across two
weightings. Each of those is
either derived from the design or is a comparison with no free constant in
it. That matters here more than usual, because the one thing a tuned
threshold would buy is exactly the thing rule 1 of this codebase forbids: a
number that decides a scientific claim and came from nowhere.

Two constants in the module ARE numbers, and both are numerical rather than
scientific, so both are recorded with their reason next to them:

* `_RCOND = 1e-10`, the singular-value cutoff in the weighted least-squares
  solve. `rcond=None` (machine epsilon) produced a leave-one-out error of
  ~2e6 on a flat six-level series, because `satexp`'s two columns go
  collinear when the held-out level is the only one in the basis's
  transition region and LAPACK's tie-break then decides the prediction. An
  inflated `satexp` error is dangerous in exactly one direction - it hands
  the comparison to `quadratic` - so this is a correctness fix, not tidiness.
* `_resolvable_lam_max = ln(100) / dz_min`, read off the design rather than
  chosen: a saturating exponential that covers 99% of its range inside one
  sampling interval is a step function as far as these levels are concerned,
  and its two coefficients are not separately determined. Above that bound
  the family is not identifiable from the data and is not the family the
  comparison is about.

The `satexp` basis is also normalised to `(1 - exp(-lam z))/(1 - exp(-lam))`
rather than the textbook `1 - exp(-lam z)`, so that it spans `[0, 1]` for
every `lam` and its `lam -> 0` limit is exactly the linear family with the
same coefficient. That changes no fit; it removes a `1/lam` blow-up in the
coefficient that made leave-one-out predictions meaningless at small `lam`.

### What an adopted verdict buys, and what it does not

An adoption says: this region's contribution to this endpoint is
NON-MONOTONE IN ITS OWN RATE, with a turning point somewhere inside the drive
range the experiment covered. It does NOT say where the turning point is in
RATE units, and cannot. The experiments measure microamps or nanomoles; the
conversion to a Wilson-Cowan rate is the transduction `r(u)`, which none of
them measured and which this codebase does not have. So
`NonlinearTerm.peak_rate` carries the same `ILLUSTRATIVE` label every P7.1
weight carries, defaults to the network's resting rate 0.5 for want of
anything measured, and P7.3 fits it. **The form is what the data buys; the
location is not.** Removing that label without a calibration for that
specific parameter is the same offence as removing an illustrative weight,
and the same rule covers it.

The readout becomes

    s = sum_{i linear} w_i r_i + sum_{j nonlinear} w_j f_j(r_j)

with `f_j` a U or inverted-U basis mapping `[0, 1] -> [0, 1]` exactly as a
rate does, so the two sums stay on one scale and P7.1's `sum |w| == 1`
normalisation is untouched. The polarity lives entirely in the basis's shape
rather than in the weight's sign, so a nonlinear term's magnitude is `+1`
like every other P7.1 term and there is still nothing for a fitted number to
quietly become.

An endpoint with nothing adopted resolves to a plain
`behavior.BehaviorReadout` - constructed as one, not merely equal to one -
so P7.1's object is what comes back, and a test asserts it by `type(...) is`.

### The adoption list is derived, never written down

`adopted_nonlinearities()` recomputes the comparison from `SERIES` rather
than reading a table of answers. There is no second copy of the verdict to
drift out of step with the data, and a test re-derives the whole set from
scratch and compares. This is the same reasoning that made P7.1 derive
`EndpointTerm.sign` from `activity` and `measure` instead of accepting a
`sign=` argument, and it matters more here, because a verdict is the output
of a fit and a fit is exactly the kind of thing that gets edited once and
recorded twice.

### What the search actually found, which is the result

Five graded single-region series with per-level numbers outside a figure,
from four papers, covering three of the seven endpoints. That is the whole
harvest of a search that, across six parallel sweeps, downloaded and
machine-screened well over 2,500 open-access full texts:

    endpoint      series                                levels  verdict
    locomotion    [Herent2023]    CnF (CUN), mouse         6     weighting-dependent
    locomotion    [Caggiano2018]  CnF (CUN), mouse         4     no-signal
    locomotion    [Caggiano2018]  PPN, mouse               4     linear-wins
    sedation      [DeLuca2022]    VLPO, mouse              5     saturating-wins-not-identifiable
    anxiety       [Diaz2011]      BLA, rat                 3     too-few-levels
    analgesia     -                                        -     no-data
    reward        -                                        -     no-data
    working_mem.  -                                        -     no-data
    gating        -                                        -     no-data

**No nonlinearity was adopted.** Not one series survived the rule, and the
five failed it in five different ways, which is a more useful outcome than
five instances of the same one. Every rejection reason in the module is
reached by real data except `turning-point-outside-range` and
`no-measured-reversal`, which are reached by the synthetic tests, and
`no-data`, which is reached by four endpoints.

### The one that came closest, and why the rule caught it

[Herent2023]'s cuneiform frequency series is the only real series that
adopted under any weighting, and it is worth reading what happened, because
it is the clearest demonstration in the task that a rule can be satisfied by
an artefact.

    5 Hz    10 Hz   15 Hz   20 Hz   30 Hz   40 Hz
    0.187   0.129   54.4    67.4    84.9    86.0     cm/s, means of 5 mice
    0.353   0.115   20.9    10.8    18.7    13.4     SD

Under uniform weights the quadratic wins leave-one-out (19.5 against
linear's 27.4), its vertex sits at 35.2 Hz, inside the range, and the means
are ordinally non-monotone. Rules 2, 3, 4 and 5 all pass. It was adopted.

The non-monotonicity is the step from 0.187 to 0.129 cm/s - a dip of
0.06 cm/s between two frequencies that, in the authors' own words, are below
the threshold for locomotor initiation and evoke essentially none. The dip is
smaller than either level's own SD. It is a floor.

Rule 5 was written to require that the MEANS turn round, and they do; it has
no notion of whether the turn is larger than the noise, by construction,
because giving it one would mean choosing a threshold. Rule 6 - agreement
across the two weightings - is what catches this, and it catches it for the
right reason rather than by luck: `1/SEM^2` is precisely the statement that a
0.06 cm/s difference between two levels with SDs of 0.35 and 0.12 is not a
difference, and under that weighting the straight line wins.

So the module's two dispersion-blind rules were both satisfied by noise at a
floor, and the dispersion-aware requirement is the one that rejected it. That
is the argument for rule 6 in one series, and it is why the rule is a
requirement for agreement rather than a choice of one weighting: the same
`1/SEM^2` that saves this series is the one that, applied alone, would let
those two floor levels carry four orders of magnitude more leverage than the
level where the behaviour actually appears.

### [DeLuca2022] is the brief's own worry, and it is a rejection

> Behavioral endpoints are frequently saturating or non-monotonic in dose, so
> this matters, but a nonlinear decoder that only fits better in-sample is
> overfitting and must be rejected.

The VLPO series is the saturating half of that sentence, in real data:

    sham    1 Hz    5 Hz    10 Hz   20 Hz
    32.2    33.7    48.2    53.9    59.2     % arousal probability from NREM
    3.1     2.5     4.1     6.0     11.2     SEM, n = 5

`satexp` beats the straight line more than four-fold out of sample (2.40
against 10.17 uniform, 3.27 against 10.97 weighted), under both weightings,
and it is not an in-sample artefact - it wins on held-out levels, which is
exactly what the brief asks a nonlinearity to do.

It is still rejected. A linear decoder reading a region whose rate saturates
in its own drive produces precisely this curve, and the circuit layer already
has that saturation in the Wilson-Cowan sigmoid. Adopting `satexp` here would
put a second sigmoid in front of the first and call the pair a finding. This
is the module's `saturating-wins-not-identifiable` category and it exists so
that the winning is RECORDED rather than either hidden or acted on.

The brief's sentence and the identifiability argument point in opposite
directions on this one series, and the argument wins. That disagreement is
the single most important thing in this task's record.

### Two things about [DeLuca2022] that had to be checked before it could be used

**The transduction runs the wrong way, and that is fine.** ChR2 is in lateral
hypothalamic orexin neurons; the fibre is over the VLPO. Raising the
stimulation frequency raises orexin release and LOWERS the VLPO
sleep-active rate. The first draft of the module's docstring said the
transduction is "monotone NON-DECREASING", which would have excluded this
series. The claim it actually needs is weaker: monotone, in either direction,
because an affine map of a monotone-decreasing function is still monotone and
a non-monotone `b(u)` still cannot come out of one. The docstring was
corrected rather than the series dropped.

**The polarity conversion happens once, in the open.** The sedation endpoint's
direction is "higher = MORE sedated", and the assay reports probability of
AROUSAL, so `score_sign = -1`. `DriveResponseSeries` refuses to be built
without an explicit `+1` or `-1` - `score_sign=0` raises - for the same reason
`EndpointTerm` derives its sign from `activity` and `measure` rather than
accepting one: a polarity that is not written down somewhere machine-readable
is a sign error waiting to happen, and this module has five chances to make
one.

### [Caggiano2018] and the two discrepancies in its deposit

P7.1 already cites [Caggiano2018] for the CUN locomotion term, and its
published Source Data holds the trial-level maximum speeds behind Fig. 1h.
Using them required resolving two things, and both are recorded on the series
rather than quietly fixed.

**The level column is headed "Power" and holds {5, 10, 20, 50}.** The paper's
Methods state the laser was "between 5 and 30 mW", which does not contain 50.
Its Results state that stimulation frequencies were stepped "from threshold
values around 5 Hz to maximal frequencies at 50 Hz". The column is frequency
in hertz and its header is wrong. That is an inference, it is the only
reading consistent with the paper's own two sentences, and it is written on
the series so a reader can disagree with it.

**The deposit holds 131 CnF trials where the figure legend says n = 148.** The
`n_per_level` used here is the deposit's, because the deposit is what the
numbers came from. Neither discrepancy changes a verdict - CnF comes back
`no-signal` and PPN `linear-wins` - but a deposit that disagrees with its own
paper twice is worth saying so about.

Means and SEMs are COMPUTED here from the trial-level values; the paper plots
medians with quartiles and states no per-level number. That is a derived
quantity and labelled one.

### [Diaz2011], and why a three-level series is in the library at all

Rat, intra-BLA, elevated plus maze, open-arm time printed with SEM in a
table: `7.5 +/- 3.7`, `41.7 +/- 5.5`, `104.8 +/- 16.9` seconds at 0, 1.5 and
5.0 pmol of the D3 antagonist U99194. Two independent screens - one of ~390
open-access full texts, one of 1,629 - found this to be the ONLY paper in the
open-access anxiety literature that prints per-dose EPM means outside a
figure.

It has three levels, so it is rejected as `too-few-levels` before a single
family is fitted. It is in `SERIES` anyway. A rejection that names the reason
is a more useful record than an absence, and "the one tabulated intra-BLA EPM
dose series in the literature has three doses and a 3-parameter family needs
four to be cross-validated at all" is a specific, actionable statement about
what P7.3 would need.

The table supports exactly one internal check - open, closed and junction
times partition a 300 s trial - and it passes to 0.1 s at all three doses.
That check is a test, because it is the only way a transposed digit in this
transcription could fail something.

Its per-group `n` is NOT in Table 1. The paper's light/dark section gives 6,
8 and 6 for the three groups of a DIFFERENT week's test and is internally
inconsistent about the middle one. So `n_per_level` is left unset, the
dispersion weighting uses the published SEMs directly, and the gap is on the
series rather than filled with a guess.

### The four endpoints with nothing, and P7.1's three targets

Four of seven endpoints have no usable series at all: analgesia, reward,
working memory and sensorimotor gating. Three of those four are exactly the
three cases P7.1 handed to P7.2 as its named targets, and each is unavailable
in a different way. `decoder.P71_TARGETS` records this in full; the shape of
it is:

1. **[ZhuoGebhart1997], RM, analgesia.** The flagship. A within-paper,
   within-assay, within-site reversal - low-intensity stimulation of the RVM
   facilitates the tail flick, higher intensity inhibits it, at the same 43
   of 86 sites. The 5/10/15/25 uA series was run. Its Results print only
   "from a minimal mean of 18.4 +/- 4.5% to a maximum mean of 27.3 +/- 7.3%"
   WITHOUT saying which intensity produced which, and the four values are in
   Fig. 1A. The two-point summary in Table 2 cannot substitute: facilitation
   is reported as percent change from control at a mean 11.8 uA and
   inhibition as percent of maximum possible inhibition at a mean 66.6 uA,
   which are different units, and assembling them into one series would
   require a conversion the paper does not license. **P7.2's single most
   consequential finding is that P7.1's flagship case cannot be used.**
2. **ACB and ventral CA1/SUB, gating.** P7.1's inverted U there is two points
   from two different papers, which is not a graded series. A scan of the 170
   open-access papers matching prepulse inhibition with intracerebral infusion
   tested every table for a %PPI value with a mean and SEM and returned zero.
   Ten studies were verified as qualifying on DESIGN - four dose levels across
   six or nine regions in [BakshiGeyer1998] and [Alsene2011], four across five
   subregions and two strains in [Swerdlow2007] - and all ten are figure-only.
   [BakshiGeyer1998] and [Swerdlow2007] contain no tables at all.
3. **Working memory, structurally.** [Zahrt1997] is the experiment: three
   intra-PFC D1-agonist doses against delayed-alternation accuracy, the
   canonical prefrontal inverted U. Its per-dose accuracy is in Fig. 2. Its
   one table reports perseveration and run time. P7.1's structural point - all
   six terms positive, so the readout is the mean rate over its regions and
   cannot hold an inverted U - survives P7.2 untouched.

### Rule 2 of this codebase, at the one place it bit

[Alsene2011] is the only paper in the entire gating literature that prints a
graded intracerebral dose series with SEM in a table: four doses across nine
forebrain regions. Its readout is STARTLE MAGNITUDE.

Prepulse inhibition is a ratio of two startle responses and startle magnitude
is one of the two. Using it would be substituting a different measured effect
for the one being modelled, which rule 2 forbids by name, and it would have
produced nine four-level series in one stroke - by some distance the largest
single addition available to this task. It is in `SEARCHED_AND_EMPTY` with the
reason, and a test asserts that its citation key appears on no series.

[MendoncaDosSantos2024] is the analogous case for analgesia and it fails on a
different rule. It is the only paper found anywhere that prints a graded
thermal-latency series in a table - intra-NTS NMDA and AP-7 with tail-flick
latencies and SEMs. Its Methods and Results say the middle NMDA dose was
3 nmol; its Table 1 says 6 nmol. A drive level the paper contradicts itself
about cannot be the x-axis of a fit, and picking one of the two would be
inventing the number rule 1 forbids. Two further problems would remain even if
that were resolved: every dose group is co-treated with i.p.
pentylenetetrazole, so the readout is postictal antinociception rather than a
clean single-region manipulation, and the table gives one value per group
without saying which of fourteen measured timepoints it is.

### Two series excluded on identifiability rather than availability

[Liang2023] and [Guo2023] both deposit per-animal values at five stimulation
frequencies with sleep-wake readouts - exactly the data this module wants -
and neither is in `SERIES`.

[Liang2023] illuminates supramammillary AXON TERMINALS in the medial septum.
The region whose rate is graded is not identified by that experiment: the
drive is to a projection, and which of its source and target the behaviour
follows is the question, not the answer. [DeLuca2022] is a terminal-field
manipulation too and IS used, and the difference is worth being precise
about: there, the fibre sits over the VLPO and the paper's own result is
about what happens to VLPO sleep-active neurons, so the graded region is
named by the experiment. Here it is not.

[Guo2023] is excluded twice over. Its soma arm is the parasubthalamic
nucleus, which carries no term in P7.1's sedation endpoint - a verdict about
a region the readout does not contain cannot change the readout, and adding
the region to the endpoint on the strength of a series collected to test the
decoder would be P7.1's job done backwards. Its two terminal arms do reach
regions the endpoint has (parabrachial, VTA) and fall to the same
identifiability objection as [Liang2023]. A test asserts that every series' structures are a subset of
its endpoint's regions.

### What the module does to the readouts, which is nothing

`resolve_nonlinear` exists, works, and currently returns exactly what
`Endpoint.resolve` returns for all seven endpoints - a plain
`behavior.BehaviorReadout`, asserted by `type(...) is` rather than by score
equality, because a `NonlinearReadout` with an empty `nonlinear` dict would
pass an equality check while silently replacing the object P7.1 promised
everything downstream. `examples/nonlinear_decoder.py` exercises the
nonlinear path anyway, on RM, under a heading that says COUNTERFACTUAL and a
`licensed_by` field that reads "NOTHING - demonstration".

Three mechanisms are built and unused, and each is unused for a reason worth
keeping rather than deleting:

* **`CONTEST_RESOLUTIONS`.** P7.1's `contested` flag and P7.2's reversal are
  the same phenomenon seen twice. Two studies of one region reporting
  opposite directions is what a reversal LOOKS LIKE when it is sampled at two
  drive levels by two different labs - [ZhuoGebhart1997]'s RM is contested in
  P7.1 for exactly the reason it was P7.2's flagship. So an adopted
  nonlinearity can RESOLVE a contest and re-admit a term P7.1 excluded, and
  the machinery for that is in `resolve_nonlinear`. It requires a written
  reason naming which two reports the reversal reconciles; a test asserts
  that no contest can be declared resolved without an adoption behind it. It
  is empty because nothing was adopted.
* **The shared-node block.** A node fed by an adopted term AND by a linear
  term cannot take the basis function: one scalar rate would have to pass
  through two response shapes at once. That is P7.1's sign-cancellation
  story in a new place and it is reported rather than resolved by picking one.
* **`NonlinearTerm.peak_rate`.** Labelled `ILLUSTRATIVE` and defaulted to the
  network's resting rate. Even a successful adoption would not have removed
  that label: the experiments measure microamps and nanomoles, the
  drive-to-rate transduction that would convert those into a Wilson-Cowan
  rate was never measured alongside them, and P7.3 fits it. The form is what
  the data buys; the location is not.

### What P7.2 delivered, checked against the standing discipline

- **A model comparison on held-out data, per endpoint, for all seven.** Three
  endpoints have series and a real comparison; four have a searched-and-empty
  record naming what was screened and why each candidate failed.
- **Nonlinearity adopted where it wins out of sample: nowhere.** Five series,
  five rejections, five different reasons.
- **Rejected cases documented**, at three levels: a reason code per series
  with its text in `REJECTION_REASONS`, a per-endpoint prose record in
  `SEARCHED_AND_EMPTY` naming the papers that were checked and what was wrong
  with each, and `P71_TARGETS` for the three cases P7.1 specifically handed
  over.
- **The identifiability argument, stated before any code**, and the asymmetry
  it produces: saturating is not evidence, non-monotone is.
- **A decision rule with no tuned constant in it.** Six rules, all of them
  either structural or a strict inequality on a held-out criterion. The two
  numeric constants in the module - `_RCOND` and `_resolvable_lam_max` - are
  numerical-linear-algebra choices with their reasons recorded, and one of
  them was a correctness fix rather than tidiness.
- **Rule 5 added after rule 4 failed a test**, with the six numbers that broke
  it kept as a test rather than described; rule 6 added after [Herent2023]
  passed rules 2-5 on a 0.06 cm/s dip between two floor levels.
- **The adoption list derived from the comparison**, never written down, and
  re-derived from scratch by a test.
- **Fifteen citations, every bibliographic prefix regenerated from PubMed's
  own esummary record**, following P7.1's discipline and re-checkable with the
  same `scripts/verify_pmids.py`. All fifteen PMIDs were verified to resolve
  to the paper claimed.
- **Nothing in P7.1 changed.** No weight, no sign, no term, no test. The
  module reads `endpoints` and does not write to it.
- **Tests.** A new `tests/test_decoder.py`, splitting into the decision rule
  (checked on synthetic series whose shape is known by construction), the
  numerics (properties that hold for any data), and the data (each published
  number pinned, so a transcription error fails a test rather than a verdict).
  None slow, none skipped, no existing test touched.
- **Outputs**: `examples/nonlinear_decoder.py` and
  `scripts/report_decoder.py` -> `results/decoder_comparison.txt`.

### What P7.3 needs that P7.2 could not get

Stated concretely, because "we found nothing" is not actionable and this is:

* **Thomas & Hammond 1995** (JPET 275:274-284, PMID 7562560). NRM and
  NGCpalpha, R(+)-baclofen over 0.1-150 ng, tail flick AND hot plate, and the
  abstract states the reversal outright: latencies rise at 0.1-1.0 ng and
  return to control by 30-50 ng. A published, graded, within-region,
  both-assay reversal in rat. JPET returns 403 to every automated route and
  the paper has no PMC deposit. This is the single highest-value unreachable
  document in the search.
* **[ZhuoGebhart1997] Fig. 1A**, four per-intensity means. Everything else
  about that paper is in reach.
* **[Zahrt1997] Fig. 2**, three per-dose accuracies.
* **[Kroeger2018] Fig. 2c**, six per-frequency NREM percentages, for the VLPO
  term this endpoint weights most heavily.
* **The two Shizgal deposits** for reward, which are real trial-level data at
  the right resolution behind an undocumented `.DAT`/`.PRM` format. URLs are
  in `SEARCHED_AND_EMPTY["reward"]`. Writing that parser is a different kind
  of task from transcribing a table and carries a different kind of error,
  which is why it was not done here rather than done badly.
* **Li 2022** (Science), a full 5 x 5 frequency-by-power matrix in LH
  hypocretin neurons whose per-condition statistics are in a non-open-access
  SI appendix.

The pattern across all six sweeps is one fact: this literature plots
everything. Designs are abundant and numbers are not, and the constraint on
P7.2 was never the method, the criterion or the code. It was that a bar chart
is not a source.

### The five mutations, and the one that changed nothing

Every defence in the module was reverted in turn and the suite re-run, in the
discipline P7.1 established when it found its own sign test to be
tautological:

    mutation                                        test that went red
    delete rule 5 (the ordinal check)               ..._vertex_falls_just_inside_...
    delete rule 4 (turning point in range)          ..._turning_point_outside_range_...
    delete rule 6 (adopt if EITHER weighting does)  ..._both_weightings_are_run_...
    delete `_resolvable_lam_max`                    ..._satexp_stays_finite_...
    change [Herent2023]'s 15 Hz mean 54.4 -> 45.4   ..._published_numbers_...

The fifth is the interesting one. Corrupting a transcribed number by 17% left
`test_each_series_has_the_verdict_its_shape_implies` GREEN - the verdict does
not change - and only the test that restates the published values a second
time caught it. That is the argument for having that test at all: a rule
robust enough to survive a corrupted input is also blind enough not to report
one, so the numbers have to be pinned separately from the conclusions drawn
from them.

### One test that is a pin and says so

`test_each_series_has_the_verdict_its_shape_implies` holds a table of the
five reasons and compares it against `assess_series`. Its first docstring
claimed the table had been "read off the published numbers by hand before the
comparison was run". That was not true - it was written after the first run -
and the claim is precisely the kind of thing P7.1's review caught in its own
sign test: a check that reads one thing twice, described as reading two
things once. The docstring now says what the test is, which is a regression
pin that makes any verdict change a deliberate edit, and points at the two
tests that can actually catch a wrong rule (the synthetic ones, where the
true shape is known by construction) and a wrong number (the transcription
test, which restates the values independently and which the fifth mutation
above confirmed is the only thing standing between a corrupted input and a
silently unchanged conclusion).

## Phase 7: fitting the endpoints against real dose-response data (P7.3)

> **P11.3 (2026-08-24):** every target this task fitted was rodent and moved
> to `legacy/behavioral_evidence.py`, so `endpoint_calibration.TARGETS` is
> empty again. The fit machinery stays, exercised on explicitly-labelled
> synthetic targets (`synthetic_target`, `synthetic_target_from_curve`),
> including a recovery test that regenerates a known gain from synthetic
> observations through the real sampler. What the task established about
> identifiability - one contrast gives a rank-one information matrix, a
> graded series lifts it - is a property of the machinery and survives the
> retirement untouched.

### The sentence in the brief, and the three things it needs at once

> Fit each behavioral endpoint against real published dose-response curves
> through the Phase 1 PK bridge, extending the P2.1 evidence module to cover
> all seven endpoints and the full drug set ... remove the illustrative label
> only from parameters actually fit.

Three things have to be true for one endpoint to be fitted, and the whole
task is the bookkeeping of which of them fails where:

1. **A dataset**: real, published, in a species and by a route `drug_pk`
   models, with per-group numbers and a dispersion outside a figure.
2. **A forward model that reaches the endpoint**: dose → brain concentration
   → occupancy → *regional rates* → the P7.1 readout. This did not exist.
   Every piece did; nothing composed them.
3. **Something identifiable at the end of it**: a published behavioural
   number is in seconds or counts, the model's readout is in rates, and what
   connects them is an unknown scale.

Condition 3 is the one this task turns on, and it is worth stating before any
data, because it decides what counts as a usable dataset:

> a two-point contrast (vehicle, one dose) cannot separate a circuit gain
> from an assay scale.

Write the behavioural measure as `b = k·A`, `A` the model's endpoint index,
`k` unknown. One drug group gives one number: two unknowns, one equation.
P2.2 got past this by assuming `k` away — with the same `k` in both groups
the drug/vehicle **ratio** is `A_drug/A_vehicle` and `k` cancels — and P7.3
inherits that assumption and its cost. What a *dose-response curve* buys over
a contrast is that the ratio is then over-determined, so the model's shape is
tested rather than merely fitted. That is why P7.3's search criterion was
"three or more dose levels in a table", and why finding exactly one such
series is the single most consequential fact in this section.

### What did not exist: dose in, endpoint out

`calibration/circuit_forward.py` (P2.2) answers "given one occupancy and one
gain, what does a three-node hand-built scenario's readout do?". Its networks
are populations (`VTA_GABA`, `CeA`), so no P7.1 endpoint can be read on them:
`Endpoint.resolve` maps CCF acronyms onto node names and a hand-built
scenario has none.

`calibration/endpoint_forward.py` is P7.3's composition, and it is a
composition rather than an implementation — the network is P3.2's build, the
operating point is P3.4's `stability.stabilize`, the densities are P4.2's
`relative_density`, the steady state is `circuit_forward.steady_state_rates`
(network-agnostic, previously exercised only at 3–5 nodes), and the readout
is P7.1's `ResolvedEndpoint`. On the 291-region Knox build every node **is**
a CCF acronym, so all seven endpoints resolve with **nothing unmapped**,
which is what makes a P7.3 fit a fit of the endpoint rather than of a
scenario that happens to share a region with it.

Two mechanisms are supported because the codebase already has two:
`drive_coupling` (the mu-opioid scenarios: the receptor adds drive to the
region it sits in, scaled by that region's density) and
`connection_modulation` (the benzodiazepine mechanism: it scales inhibitory
synapses, so the density that matters is the *postsynaptic* region's). Both
carry P4.2's factorization `coupling[region] = mechanism_gain · ρ[region]`,
which means **`mechanism_gain` is the only free parameter in the whole
chain**: PK, partition and Ki are calibrated, ρ is measured, and everything
downstream is P7.1's cited membership and sign.

### The reduction that makes the fit affordable, and that it is exact

The gain and the activation enter only as their **product**:

    drive_i  = baseline_i + gain·ρ_i·activation
    W_ij    <- W_ij · (1 + gain·ρ_i·activation)          (W_ij < 0)

so the steady state is a function of the single scalar `x = gain·activation`.
This is exact, not approximate, and
`test_only_the_product_of_gain_and_activation_matters` pins it by evaluating
three (gain, activation) pairs with the same product and requiring identical
rates. It matters because one 291-node steady state costs 2–7 s: a
`ResponseCurve` over a grid of `x` is computed once and interpolated inside
the sampler. The interpolation is linear rather than spline — a cubic can
overshoot between grid points and put a value the circuit cannot produce into
a likelihood — and its error is **measured** against a re-integration at the
grid midpoints rather than assumed: 1.4e-05 to 4.9e-05 on the 291-region
curve, against likelihood widths of 0.05 to 0.29. Three orders of magnitude
below the smallest published uncertainty is the sense in which an
interpolated prediction and an integrated one are the same datum.

### The index, and the zero a ratio needs

P2.2's readout was one node's firing rate, where zero means something. A P7.1
endpoint score is not that. It is `Σ w_i r_i` with signs on both sides and
`Σ|w_i| = 1`, so at the drug-free rest state (P3.4 balances every node to
r = 0.5) it is `0.5·Σ w_i`: **+0.5 for working memory, −0.375 for sedation,
+0.1 for analgesia.** A ratio of a quantity whose zero is an accident of
which regions happened to be cited is not something any assay can be compared
with, and analgesia's +0.1 would have been a near-zero denominator.

`endpoint_forward.directed_activity_index` is the answer:

    A = Σ_{w>0} w_i r_i + Σ_{w<0} |w_i| (1 − r_i) = score + Σ_{w<0}|w_i|

the fraction of the endpoint's cited evidence currently pointing towards
*more* of the behaviour. Bounded in [0, 1]; zero means every pro-behaviour
region silent and every anti-behaviour region saturated; and at rest it is
**exactly 0.5 for all seven endpoints**, because `Σ|w| = 1` and `r = 0.5`.
A test asserts that for all seven rather than this paragraph claiming it.
It is still an assumption — it puts a linear readout's zero where all the
evidence points the wrong way — and it is declared on the function.

### The evidence: all seven endpoints, and what the searches actually found

`behavioral_evidence.ENDPOINT_COVERAGE` is the acceptance criterion as a
computable object: seven records, checked against `endpoints.ENDPOINTS` and
against this module's own entry keys by `endpoint_coverage()`, so an endpoint
cannot be silently omitted and a record cannot name an entry that does not
exist. The module grew from 5 entries to 11.

| endpoint | verdict | evidence |
|---|---|---|
| locomotion | fit-attempted | [Sagara2008] 3 doses + vehicle, IP, n=10, SEM; [Graziani2022] open field |
| anxiety | fit-attempted | [Graziani2022] EPM (P2.2's target), [Stickling2024], [Pellow1985] |
| analgesia | fit-attempted | [Lustyk2023] 2 doses + vehicle, IP, hot plate; [Yassen2008] concentration-response |
| sedation | fit-attempted | [Graziani2022] immobility; [Obert2025] 4 IV doses; [Kissin1983] quantal ED50 |
| reward | **no-data** | — |
| working memory | **no-data** | — |
| sensorimotor gating | **no-data** | — |

The constraint that shapes all of this is narrower than "what has been
published". `drug_pk` builds exactly four (drug, species, route) triples —
fentanyl/rat/IV, haloperidol/rat/IV, diazepam/rat/IV and diazepam/rat/IP —
and of those, **exactly one reaches a receptor**: `BehavioralEvidenceEntry.
receptor_drive_status()`, added here, asks `drug_pk` whether the
plasma-to-brain step yields an *unbound* brain concentration, and for
fentanyl the answer is `total-brain-only`. P1.5 already recorded why (no rat
brain unbound fraction for fentanyl exists, so its Kp of ~16.5 is mostly
tissue binding and "must not drive receptor occupancy"), but no earlier task
had to care, because P2.1 and P2.2's bridgeable entries were both diazepam.
P7.3 is the task where that gap decides an endpoint.

### The one graded series, and why a null is the useful kind

**[Sagara2008]** (J Pharmacol Sci 2008;107(3):355–60, PMID 18603833, open
access) prints diazepam 0.2/0.5/1.0 mg/kg IP against vehicle, ANIMEX
locomotor counts over 10 min, 15 min after dosing, n = 10 per group, in a
table: 153.6 ± 16.6, 156.5 ± 22.9, 158.3 ± 24.6, 161.7 ± 19.1. Nothing moves.

That is the only graded, tabulated, bridgeable behavioural dose-response
found for any of the seven endpoints, and it is a null. A null with error bars
is not an absence *in principle*: the model predicts that potentiating
inhibition brain-wide *lowers* the locomotion index monotonically in the gain,
so three doses that move nothing would put an **upper bound** on that gain,
the same one-sided verdict shape P2.3 reached for
`gaba_a_connection_modulation_gain` from the other side.

**In practice it does not, and the committed fit is what says so.** The first
draft of this section claimed the upper bound as a result; the run in
`results/calibration/endpoint_fits.txt` refutes it, and the claim is
withdrawn rather than kept as an intention. At the largest gain the prior
allows, the whole-brain locomotion index falls by 4.7–6.4% across the three
doses (model ratios 0.9530, 0.9415, 0.9361), against SEM-derived widths of
17–20% on the observed ratios (1.0189 ± 0.185, 1.0306 ± 0.195, 1.0527 ±
0.169). The posterior is **2.37 ± 1.43 on a Uniform(0, 5) prior whose own
mean is 2.5 and sd 1.44**, which is the prior to two digits, with an 89%
interval of [0.25, 4.70], and `bound_verdict` returns `wrong-direction`, because the
counts rose slightly rather than falling.

The cause lies in the model rather than in the dataset: refutation 2 again,
arriving through the one series that was supposed to be immune to it. P3.4's
illustrative ρ = 0.9 sets `weight_scale = 0.0201`, so a gain of 5 moves the
index by ~6% where the data resolve ~18%. A graded null can only bound a
model that *can* move. The
`tests/test_endpoint_calibration.py::test_a_null_series_pushes_the_gain_down_
rather_than_up` test still shows the mechanism working on a synthetic curve
with a real slope, which is the right place for that claim to live: it is a
statement about the rule, not about this data set against this operating
point.

So the corrected summary of the task is sharper than the original and worse
for the model: **no target in P7.3 identifies anything.** [Graziani2022]'s EPM
contrast moves the right way and ~6× too little; its open-field contrast, read
as locomotion and again as sedation, moves the wrong way; and the two graded
nulls, which were the targets that could have produced a one-sided bound,
fail because the index moves 2.8–6.4% where the data resolve 17–21%. All five
posteriors are either pinned on a prior bound or identical to the prior. The
one-sided identification stays a property of the rule, demonstrated on a
synthetic curve in the tests, until the operating point lets the model move.

**[Lustyk2023]** (Neurochem Res 2023;48(3):839–51, PMC9644393) is the second
graded series: diazepam 5 and 10 mg/kg IP against 52.5 °C hot-plate latency,
30 min, means and **SDs** — the only entry in the module reported that way,
and the reason `DISPERSION_KINDS` records the kind rather than normalising
it. A ratio of group means needs the sd *of the mean*, so the caller divides
by √n at the point of use, and the source gives n as a band (6–9) rather than
per group, so the defensible choice is the smallest, which gives the widest
width and therefore the weakest constraint. Also a null (the paper's own
F(2,20) = 1.409, ns).

### Four refutations, each measured rather than argued

**1. The sign, for locomotion and sedation.** [Graziani2022]'s rats crossed
38% *more* lines under diazepam. A whole-brain potentiation of inhibition can
only lower the locomotion index, at any gain of either sign inside a
mechanistically bounded prior. `bound_verdict` returns `wrong-direction` and
the posterior piles on the mechanistic null at zero. The same contrast read
as sedation (immobility fell where the model needs it to rise) fails
identically — which is honest to report as *one* contrast counted twice
rather than as two independent failures, because it is the same four animals
in the same five minutes.

**2. The sensitivity, for anxiety.** The model moves the right way and not
far enough. At a gain of 5 — a 5.5-fold potentiation of every inhibitory
synapse in the brain, far beyond any benzodiazepine — the whole-brain anxiety
index moves from 0.5 to 0.4804, a ratio of 0.964 against [Graziani2022]'s
measured 0.7835 ± 0.0517. The best achievable prediction misses by 3.5 of the
observation's own standard deviations. This is a statement about the
**operating point**, not about the data: P3.4's illustrative ρ = 0.9 sets
`weight_scale = 0.0201`, so every inhibitory weight is 50× smaller than the
published density, and scaling something 50× too small by (1 + g·a) barely
moves anything. The three-node amygdala scenario reproduces the same
published anxiolysis at a gain of 0.074 (P2.2) precisely because its one
synapse was hand-set to be consequential. **The disagreement between the two
is the most useful single number in this task**, and it belongs to P3.4 and
P9, not to P7.1.

**3. The steepness, for analgesia.** [Yassen2008] — already this codebase's
fentanyl rat IV PK source — publishes its antinociception as a logistic
regression in the biophase concentration, `P = 1/(1+exp(−(α + β·Ce)))` with
α = −8.77 (95% CI −11.49 to −6.05) and β = 1.11 per ng/mL (0.726–1.494), from
486 observations in 40 rats. It needs **no dose bridge at all**. Its curve
rises from 10% to 90% over a **1.67-fold** concentration span; a one-site
occupancy curve needs **81-fold**, for every drug and every Kd, because
occupancy is C/(C+Kd). No monotone function of fractional occupancy is that
steep, so no linear readout over occupancy-driven rates can reproduce this
dataset at any gain. The steepness is partly an artefact of a *quantal*
endpoint — a probability of crossing a 10 s cut-off is steepened by
between-animal variance — and modelling that honestly needs a threshold and a
spread, i.e. two more free parameters against a curve that publishes two.
Three parameters, two constraints: underdetermined by exactly one, which is a
counted degeneracy rather than a judgement.

**4. Monotone invariance, for sedation's two intravenous curves.** Sedation
is the one endpoint with a real IV dose-response, and there are two.
[Obert2025] gives four IV fentanyl doses against the time to return of the
righting reflex (13, 15, 26, 50 min at 12.5, 25, 50, 100 µg/kg);
[Kissin1983] gives a quantal ED50 of 0.023 mg/kg (95% fiducial limits
0.020–0.026) for losing it. Both measure a **threshold-crossing time or
dose**, and every stage between plasma concentration and the endpoint index —
occupancy, the Wilson-Cowan steady state, the linear readout — is monotone,
so the crossing is preserved exactly. Four latencies therefore constrain
*one* number, where the threshold sits on the concentration axis, and say
nothing whatever about the endpoint's regional weights. **These datasets
calibrate `drug_pk`, not `endpoints`**, and are recorded as such. This is the
one refutation in the task that would survive every other blocker being
fixed.

### The fits, and their diagnostics

Five targets, one free parameter each (`gaba_a_whole_brain_modulation_gain`,
uniform on [0, 5] with both bounds taken from the mechanism exactly as P2.2
argued for its own), sampled with `DEMetropolisZ`, 4 chains × 1000 tune ×
1000 draws, seed 20260814. `scripts/run_endpoint_fits.py` →
`results/calibration/endpoint_fits.txt`, per-target summaries and posteriors
alongside, and `endpoint_fit_diagnostics.csv`.

RESULTS_TABLE_PLACEHOLDER

Every fit converged. **None of them licenses a number**, and the module says
so in three independent ways rather than leaving it to be read off a
posterior: `bound_verdict` (is the observation inside the model's reach at
all?), `best_residual_sd` (how far is the *best* prediction in the box, in
units of the published uncertainty?), and `information_matrix` (what can a
dataset of this shape identify?). The last is P2.3's method at a different
scale: for a single Gaussian observation `F = s sᵀ/sd²` is rank one whatever
`s` is, so a two-point contrast cannot separate a gain from a scale — the
measured eigenvalue ratio is ~1e-20, i.e. machine zero — while a three-level
series lifts that rank, which is exactly what "a dose-response curve buys
something a contrast does not" means, expressed as a spectrum.

### What P7.3 changed, and what it deliberately did not

**No illustrative label was removed, anywhere.** Not one endpoint weight, not
`MU_OPIOID_MECHANISM_GAIN`, not P3.4's operating gain, not P4.2's
proportionality. `gaba_a_whole_brain_modulation_gain` is deliberately **not**
in `priors.PRIOR_SPECS`: that module's `CIRCUIT_LAYER_PARAM_EVIDENCE_KEYS` is
the register of circuit-layer parameters this project *has* calibrated,
guarded by a test that requires each of them to name a calibration-ready
dataset, and putting a bound-limited posterior there would be claiming a
calibration that did not happen. A test asserts it stays out, and another
asserts that no endpoint's coverage record reads `fitted`, so a later pass
that does fit one has to change that test in the same commit that removes the
label — rule 3 of this codebase, expressed as an assertion.

P2.2's `gaba_a_connection_modulation_gain` is untouched and is a **different
parameter**: one synapse in a three-node circuit against every inhibitory
connection in a 291-region brain, weighted by Gabra1 density. They are not
comparable and neither is evidence about the other. A test pins that too.

### Three corrections to this repository's own record

Rule 1 applies to numbers copied from our own prose, and P7.3 re-ran the
searches P2.2 recorded rather than inheriting them.

1. **[Wadenberg2000] is not a haloperidol study.** P2.2's section names
   Wadenberg et al., Psychopharmacology 2000;150(4):422–9 (PMID 10958084) as
   one of "the two papers that do exactly this" for haloperidol occupancy
   versus behaviour, and calls obtaining it "the single cheapest thing that
   would unblock this system". Its abstract, re-read here, is about
   **raclopride** throughout ("cold raclopride (0.01–0.2 mg/kg) produced
   16–77% D2 receptor occupancy and no catalepsy"). Haloperidol appears
   nowhere in its design. It fails rule 2 on drug identity before access is
   even a question, and its endpoints (catalepsy, conditioned avoidance) are
   outside the seven besides. The paper remains closed; that no longer
   matters.
2. **[Johnson2014] contains no measured occupancy.** The other of P2.2's two
   named papers (Pharm Res 2014;31(10):2605–17) was obtained in full here.
   Its own Methods say "it was not possible to measure D2RO in the same
   animals and plasma drug concentrations were not available for these rats";
   every occupancy in it is *simulated* from earlier PBPK/PD models, its
   behavioural endpoint is catalepsy, and its strain is stated only as "Wiga
   SPF rats" with sex never given. The measured-occupancy data it rests on
   are in Johnson 2011 (PMC3170473) and Kozielska 2012.
3. **The fentanyl PD paper P2.2 quoted from an abstract has an intercept.**
   P2.2 recorded [Yassen2008]'s odds ratio (3.03) and T½,ke0 (6.08 min),
   which fix the curve's slope and lag and leave its position on the
   concentration axis undetermined. The full text gives α = −8.77, and with
   it the whole curve — which is what made refutation 3 above computable.
